name: DM_AB
meaning: `=<frames>` splits the run into phases of that many frames and alternates every switch set to `ab` (on in the odd phases); logs an `[ab]` line per phase with GPU and frame time and attachment traffic

name: DM_ALIAS_SIZE
meaning: `=<bytes>` gives the guest an alias region of that size instead of the profile's (at least 256 MB, whole host pages; the heap and stacks stay as they are): `0x1000000000`, the Switch's 64 GB, holds what a game reserves unchanged; the NSP script's address region check sets it (Mac only: an iPhone has no room)

name: DM_ALIAS_WINDOWS
meaning: `=<MB>` logs every 30 s how much of each window of that size in the alias region is mapped (windows aligned to their size in absolute addresses)

name: DM_ALLOW_OTHER_METAL
meaning: `1` lets `own_compilers.py` build the shader libraries with a Metal compiler other than the one in `dmsh_chain.lock` (it stops otherwise, GitHub issue #242); the NSP script sets it for `--allow-other-metal`

name: DM_AOC_DIR
meaning: Folder of add-on content: one numbered subfolder per DLC index holding that DLC's RomFS, reported by `aoc` and mounted read-only; the app, the Mac launcher and the NSP script set it when the build has DLC

name: DM_AOC_OWNED
meaning: `0` reports no add-on content even when `DM_AOC_DIR` has some, for runs without the DLC

name: DM_APP_VERSION
meaning: Overrides the IPA's version in `build_ipa.sh`; by default it is the packed game's display version from its control data (the update's when one is packed)

name: DM_AUDIO
meaning: `1` plays audio through Core Audio, `0` uses the silent sink; real output is the default on iOS, the silent sink on the Mac (the Mac launcher sets `1`)

name: DM_AUDIO_BLOCKS
meaning: `=<n>` keeps n 5 ms blocks in flight from the CPU audio renderer to the output (2 to 32, default 12 = 60 ms): more absorbs a render thread that comes late, each block adds 5 ms of latency

name: DM_AUDIO_DEVICE_MS
meaning: `=<ms>` (Android) the AAudio output stream's buffer in ms (1 to 200, default 40; whole bursts, at least two, at most the stream's capacity). Two bursts (8 ms on the POCO F8 Pro) left the shared stream empty whenever the callback thread came late: audible drop-outs while the renderer's queue never ran dry. Each report line also counts the stream's own underruns (AAudioStream_getXRunCount)

name: DM_AUDIO_DUMP
meaning: `=<file>` writes every PCM block the game appends as is (16-bit, 48 kHz, channel count as in the OpenAudioOut log), to judge whether a sound played

name: DM_AUDIO_MUTE
meaning: `=1` runs the real Core Audio output path (callback pacing, background take-over) with the output silenced, for lifecycle tests on the Mac without noise

name: DM_AUDREN_GATE_MS
meaning: `=<ms>` (0 to 5, default 2) a frame the CPU audio renderer renders from its backlog (it woke up late) waits that long at most for the game's RequestUpdate after the frame before it, while 3 or more blocks are still queued for the output, as the audio DSP leaves the game an update between 5 ms frames; `0` renders the backlog back to back (the old behaviour, which advanced every voice by several frames on one game state)

name: DM_AUDREN_NICE
meaning: `=<n>` (Linux / Android) the CPU audio renderer's render thread's nice value (-20 to 19, default -16, Android's THREAD_PRIORITY_AUDIO); `keep` leaves the guest thread default (-4)

name: DM_AUDREN_TRACE
meaning: When set, the CPU audio renderer logs every update with the number of frames rendered since the previous one

name: DM_AUDREN_UPDATE_NICE
meaning: `=<n>` (Linux / Android, -20 to 19) gives the game thread that calls the audio renderer's RequestUpdate (its audio frame thread, which refills the voices) that nice value; unset leaves it as it is

name: DM_AUDREN_WATCH
meaning: `=<name>,<name>…` (Android, up to 6 guest thread names) adds those threads' CPU time, time runnable but waiting for a CPU and major page faults over each audio renderer report to its `audren threads` line, beside the RequestUpdate thread's

name: DM_BOOTPROF
meaning: When set, logs boot timing: the loader's breakdown (mapping, relocation, probes), Metal library loading, pipeline creation, texture uploads and the first present

name: DM_BUILD_COMMIT
meaning: The commit the build was made from, which the host logs at start-up; the Android launcher sets it from the commit Gradle stamped into the APK (the Apple apps read `DMCommit` from Info.plist instead)

name: DM_BUNDLE_ID
meaning: Overrides the iOS app's bundle ID in `build_ipa.sh` (default `org.nxnative.<title ID in lowercase>`)

name: DM_CHEATS
meaning: Folder of Atmosphère cheat files: `<folder>/<build ID>.txt` or an SD-card layout (`atmosphere/contents/<title ID>/cheats/`) under it (default `<DM_ROOT>/cheats`); the Mac menu lists and toggles them

name: DM_CHEATS_ANY_BUILD
meaning: `1` loads a cheat file written for another build of the game when it is the only one (its addresses may not fit: for `cheat_anchor.py` checks)

name: DM_CHEATS_DEBUG
meaning: Logs every memory write a cheat makes and the cheat file context the menu's "another version" rows come from

name: DM_CHEATS_ON
meaning: Comma-separated cheat names turned on at launch, besides the saved per-build enabled states

name: DM_CHEATS_WINDOW
meaning: `1` opens the Mac Cheats panel beside the game from the start

name: DM_COPY_GAME_RESOURCES
meaning: `NO` skips the Xcode build phase that copies the game's resources into the app (`stage_resources.sh`, on by default); `build_ipa.sh` sets it for its unsigned build, which packs them itself

name: DM_COPY_ROMFS
meaning: `NO` keeps the game files out of the app, in the Xcode build phase (`stage_resources.sh`) and in the unsigned IPA of `build_ipa.sh` (on by default): `main.m` takes the validated `Documents/romfs.img` copied by `scripts/push_romfs.sh`, then a `Documents/romfs` folder; the build writes the image's identity as `romfs.id` into the app, and `main.m` uses only a matching image (`--romfs separate` of the NSP script sets this)

name: DM_CTL
meaning: `=<file>` (Mac): the host polls the file every 100 ms and runs each appended line: button presses, `shot`, `passdump`, `texdump`, `env KEY=VALUE`, `peek`, `memdump`, `drag` and more

name: DM_DBG
meaning: When set, prints the guest's `svcOutputDebugString` text to stderr as `[guest]` lines

name: DM_DBG_AU_FRAMES
meaning: `=<frames>` asks the Mac's Core Audio output for that many frames per callback instead of about 5 ms (1024 reproduces the iOS default that caused crackling)

name: DM_DETCLOCK
meaning: `=<step ns>`: from the first present on, the guest clock advances a fixed step per present instead of following the wall clock, and the random source becomes a fixed-seed stream (replay and test runs)

name: DM_DETCLOCK_PACE
meaning: `=1` with `DM_DETCLOCK`: each frame takes at least one clock step of wall time, so background loading keeps up with the fixed clock (used by the screenshot gate)

name: DM_DISPLAY_NAME
meaning: Overrides the iOS app's name in `build_ipa.sh` (default the game name in the base NSP's control data)

name: DM_DYNAMIC_RESOLUTION
meaning: `1` lets NieR:Automata 1.0.3's own dynamic resolution scale between 70 and 100 %, `0` (default) keeps full resolution; only on the builds whose patches.py names the DYNAMIC_RESOLUTION capability (`hle_fpslock.c` `k_nier_dr`). The launcher's Dynamic resolution

name: DM_ENTITLEMENTS
meaning: `=<plist>` gives a prepared Xcode project another entitlements file instead of the Increased Memory Limit one, and the ad-hoc signature of the unsigned IPA's executable carries them; empty means no entitlements

name: DM_ENV_FILE
meaning: `=<file>` makes `build_ipa.sh` bake its `KEY=VALUE` lines into the app as `dm/env.txt`, applied at boot; `Documents/env.txt` overrides them

name: DM_ENV_FILE_KEYS
meaning: Set by the iOS app and the Mac launcher at launch to the space-separated names an env file set; the settings screen keeps those values and shows them greyed out

name: DM_ENV_LAUNCH_KEYS
meaning: Set at launch by the Mac launcher (the launcher settings already in the environment) and the iOS app (every DM_* variable already in it) to the space-separated names; the settings screen keeps those values and shows them greyed out

name: DM_FASTBOOT
meaning: `1` (test runs) sets the game profile's `fastboot_env` switches that are not set already: for Donkey Kong Bananza, A every 12 presented frames from the first one, `DM_MARK_DRAWS=3000` and `DM_MARK_KEYS_STOP=1`, so a run reaches the first level as fast as the game allows and logs when (android/TESTING.md, Fast test runs)

name: DM_FD_LOG
meaning: `=<seconds>` logs, every that many seconds, the number and kinds of file descriptors the process has open

name: DM_FIXED_TIME
meaning: `=<seconds>`: the user clock always returns that time and the host time zone is pinned to UTC, for deterministic comparison

name: DM_FONT_DIR
meaning: Folder of the shared-font stand-ins (`standard.ttf`, `nintendo_ext.ttf` with the button icons); the app, the Mac launcher and the NSP script set it

name: DM_FORCE_STRICT
meaning: `=1` makes the loader fail on forced-hook entries no module references, instead of only noting them (for checking a mistyped list)

name: DM_FPS
meaning: `30` or `60` pins the frame rate the display link and frame pacing aim for; otherwise it follows the game's present interval (60, or 30 when the game asks for 30)

name: DM_FPS_HOLD
meaning: `on` / `off` overrides the profile's `fps_hold`: whether late frames may raise the hold above the frame cap's vsyncs (on by default)

name: DM_FPS_TARGET
meaning: Frame-rate cap: `30` or `60`, or `0` for the game's own limit; overrides the profile's `fps_target`

name: DM_FS
meaning: When set, logs file opens, paths not found or not mounted, and a read summary every 64 MiB or 1000 reads

name: DM_FSLOG
meaning: `=<file>` writes one TSV line per ReadFile: seconds since boot, guest path, offset, length and guest buffer address

name: DM_FSLOG_HASH
meaning: With `DM_FSLOG`, adds a column with the FNV-1a 64 hash of the bytes read

name: DM_FSTEP_LOG_S
meaning: `=<s>` (restart, 0; Ocarina of Time 10 in its profile) with the frame step on (`fps_target`, a FRAME_STEP stub), a `frame step: last … s` line every s seconds: frames and fps, the step handed to the game per frame (1 / 2 / 3 / 4+ vsyncs, mean), the hold, the debt and game time against real time (the stubs' count)

name: DM_FULLSCREEN
meaning: `1` (any value but `0`) starts the Mac window in fullscreen; `0` or unset, a window. The Mac settings window's Display mode

name: DM_GAME
meaning: Selects the game profile (a title ID under `dm/games` or `DM_GAMES_DIR`) for the Python tools and the rewriter; there is no default

name: DM_GAMES_DIR
meaning: Profile folders outside the repository, separated by `:`, searched after `dm/games`; the NSP script points it at a provisional or derived profile

name: DM_GAMES_FIRST
meaning: `=1` searches `DM_GAMES_DIR` before `dm/games`, so a provisional or derived profile wins over the game's own (the NSP script's `--provisional`)

name: DM_GAME_ENV
meaning: `KEY=VALUE` pairs, separated by spaces, that the game's own `getenv` returns, in place of the profile's `game_env` (`hle_os.c`); any other name goes to the SDK's empty environment

name: DM_GFX_FIXTURE_OUT
meaning: `=<dir>`: graphics tests write their raw result textures and buffers there

name: DM_GLSLC_CAPTURE
meaning: `=<dir>` saves every GLSLC output the game compiles at run time; `shader_split.py` reads it (default `<version dir>/glslc_capture`)

name: DM_GL_CAPTURE
meaning: `=<dir>`: the GL layer writes every shader source the game compiles (`<key>.vert` / `<key>.frag`) for `gl_shaders.py`; the NSP script uses it to capture run-time shaders

name: DM_GL_DRAWLOG
meaning: `=<n>[:<seconds>]` logs the first `<n>` GL draws after `<seconds>`, each with its framebuffer, viewport, scissor box, program, uniforms, samplers and its vertex attributes' first vertices; `=1` or more also names samplers that have no texture

name: DM_GL_FBLOG
meaning: `=1` logs every framebuffer bind with its size and the draws so far

name: DM_GL_LOG
meaning: `=1` makes the GL layer log object creation

name: DM_GL_MISSES
meaning: `=1` reports each `eglGetProcAddress` name the layer lacks when the game first asks for it

name: DM_GL_STUBS
meaning: `=1` gives every GL function the layer lacks a stub that reports its first call and returns 0, instead of a null pointer (bring-up)

name: DM_GPU_CAPTURE
meaning: `=<frame>[:<frames>]` or `gpu:<ms>[:<after frame>]` writes a Metal GPU trace of those frames for Xcode's Metal debugger; can be set while running through `DM_CTL`

name: DM_GPU_CAPTURE_DIR
meaning: Folder for `DM_GPU_CAPTURE`'s traces (default `gpu_captures/` in the working directory)

name: DM_GPU_CAPTURE_KEEP
meaning: Before each GPU capture, prunes the capture folder's `dm_*.gputrace` entries so that the newest `KEEP - 1` stay (default 2)

name: DM_GPU_TURBO
meaning: `1` (Android, live, default 0) the device-wide KGSL GPU turbo: `KGSL_PROP_PWRCTRL` = 0 on `/dev/kgsl-3d0` turns the kernel's GPU clock scaling off (the highest clock the thermal limits allow) from the next submission until the queue is drained (a suspend, a swapchain change), exit or `0`; each change is logged with the kernel's answer. Risks: more heat and power, so the thermal cap may come sooner; it is device-wide and outlives a killed run (the next run turns the scaling back on from a `TMPDIR/dm_gpu_turbo` marker) ([frame-rate.md](reference/frame-rate.md#a-gpu-clock-capped-under-the-kgsl-floor-android-turnip))

name: DM_GRAPHICS_SCALE
meaning: The Switch 2 graphics scale the game sees in every operation mode: `0`, `1` or `2` (`oe::GetCurrentGraphicsScale`, scaling parameters 10 / 20 / 30); unset follows the operation mode (0 handheld, 1 console). Mario Kart World renders its 3D scenes smaller at a higher scale (handheld scale 2: 1280x720); read once

name: DM_GUEST_BASE
meaning: `=<hex>` where the guest address block starts on Android (default `0x4000000000`); when it is taken the host tries the next 64 GiB boundaries, always below `1 << 39`

name: DM_GUEST_SPAWN_TEST
meaning: `=1` runs a self-test before `nnMain`: a host-started guest thread does SDK malloc / free and locks an `nn::os` mutex, and the result is logged; `=2` also keeps a resident thread

name: DM_HID_LOG
meaning: `1` logs the HID button usage number of each button pressed on a raw HID gamepad (`pad_hid_mac.h`), to write a `DM_HID_MAP`

name: DM_HID_MAP
meaning: `=<map>` such as `A=1,B=2,X=4,Y=5`: which HID button usage presses each Switch button on a raw HID gamepad (names A B X Y LS RS L R ZL ZR PLUS MINUS LEFT UP RIGHT DOWN; default 8BitDo's D-input numbering by position, `pad_hid.h`); Mac only

name: DM_HID_PADS
meaning: `0` stops reading raw HID gamepads that GameController does not list, such as an 8BitDo in its own mode (`pad_hid_mac.h`); Mac only

name: DM_HITCH_DUMP
meaning: `=<ms>[:<s>]`: when no frame has been presented for that long (from s seconds on), logs every guest thread once per stall: wait, last SVC, pc, lr, frames and registers

name: DM_HLECOUNT
meaning: `=<file>` (`%d` = process ID) writes at exit a TSV of how many times the guest called each HLE function, zero counts included

name: DM_HLECOUNT_AT
meaning: `=<s>[,<s>…]` with `DM_HLECOUNT`: also writes the counts at those seconds from process start, as `<file>.<s>`; the difference of two shows what the guest calls in between (Android, where the game process is killed, never reaches the exit)

name: DM_ICON
meaning: `=<image>` gives `build_ipa.sh` another app icon (default the `icon.jpg` beside the RomFS)

name: DM_IMPORTS
meaning: When set, logs each import the loader binds to a host function and each forced takeover

name: DM_KBD
meaning: `=<text>`: the system keyboard returns that text as OK without showing an input box; unset with no window, it returns cancel

name: DM_KBD_PLAYER
meaning: `own` makes the Mac keyboard player 1 on its own, with controllers from player 2 on (by default the first controller shares player 1 with the keyboard)

name: DM_KEYS
meaning: Scripted input: `<seconds or f<frame>>:<key>[+key][~hold or ~f<frames>][*count/interval],…` presses buttons, sticks, touches and `Shake` at those times; `=@<file>` reads the steps from the file

name: DM_LANG
meaning: Game language as a language code (default `en-US`; the iOS app sets the one the IPA was packed with)

name: DM_LAUNCHER
meaning: `0` skips the iOS settings screen or the Mac settings window and starts the game at once, with the saved choices (on the Mac also `--no-launcher`)

name: DM_LINK_VTICK
meaning: `0` keeps the system's display-link rate on 144 or 165 Hz Mac screens; by default the link counts only the refreshes nearest a steady 1/60 s clock

name: DM_LOADHASH
meaning: `=1` logs an address-independent SHA-256 per module after loading

name: DM_LONGFRAME
meaning: `0` turns off the long-frame log (on by default), a line for a frame over 20 ms or with GPU time over 16.7 ms that is clearly above recent frames

name: DM_LONGFRAME_FAULTS
meaning: `1` (Android, restart, off): with `DM_LONGFRAME_THREADS`, each reading also takes every thread's major page faults; the `[longframe]` line's busiest threads get theirs (`mf`) and the thread with the most, when not one of them, is named after them (`most major faults`)

name: DM_LONGFRAME_THREADS
meaning: `=<ms>` (Android, 250; `0` off, restart): a sampler thread reads every thread's run time that often, and a `[longframe]` line of a frame of 100 ms or more names the 3 busiest threads since the frame began

name: DM_LSFG
meaning: `1` / `0` (Android, live, default 0) Lossless Scaling frame generation on or off; the launcher sets it from its Frame generation setting, `env.txt` overrides it; needs `DM_LSFG_DLL`

name: DM_LSFG_DLL
meaning: `=<file>` (Android, restart) the `Lossless.dll` frame generation loads its shaders from; the launcher sets it to its private copy; unset: frame generation is unavailable

name: DM_LSFG_FLOW
meaning: `=<pct>` (Android, live, default 75) frame generation's motion estimation resolution in % (25-100; `0` auto, the game's own resolution); the launcher sets it

name: DM_LSFG_MULT
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, live, default 2) frame generation's frames per game frame, 2 to 4; the launcher sets it

name: DM_LSFG_TARGET
meaning: `=<fps>` (Android, live, default 0) a target frame rate for frame generation instead of the fixed multiplier (the multiplier follows it); `0` uses `DM_LSFG_MULT`; the launcher sets it

name: DM_MARK_DRAWS
meaning: `=<n>` logs `[mark] frame …: … draws` once, at the first of 5 frames in a row with n draws or more, in seconds from process start and on the wall clock: the time from launch to a scene (a level's 3D frames) read off the log

name: DM_MARK_KEYS_STOP
meaning: `1` drops the remaining `DM_KEYS` steps when `DM_MARK_DRAWS` logs its mark, so presses that only lead to the test scene stop there

name: DM_MEASURE_LOCK
meaning: `=<file>`: `scripts/regress.py`'s default `--lock`, the measuring lock `scripts/bench.py --lock` shares: held only while a game runs, and the harness's shader builds pause while another process holds it

name: DM_MEMSTAT
meaning: `=<tsv>` writes one line per second of memory accounting: footprint, Metal allocation and resident and charged memory by region class (guest, code, malloc, gpu, …)

name: DM_MEMSTAT_DUMP
meaning: `=<seconds>`: with `DM_MEMSTAT`, at that second writes every VM region of 1 MiB or more to `<tsv>.regions`

name: DM_MEM_CAP_GB
meaning: `=<GB>`: the memory watchdog exits when resident memory exceeds that many GB (default 24 on the Mac, none on iOS; `0` turns it off)

name: DM_MEM_FILEBACK
meaning: `1` (Android, read once, default 0; Ocarina of Time 1 in its profile) memory pools of the kinds `DM_MEM_FILEBACK_KINDS` names become, at `nvnMemoryPoolInitialize`, a shared mapping of an unlinked sparse file in TMPDIR (the app's cache folder) instead of anonymous memory, through the placement swap (range read-only, writers held, pages with data copied, `mremap` over it): clean file pages the kernel drops instead of zram; a part the GPU is given later is placed as before (its file range punched), what is left goes back to anonymous memory at Finalize; `[vk] file-backed pools:` lines give MiB moved and read back, the file's blocks on disk, the process's write_bytes, failures ([RED]: the pool stays anonymous with its bytes) (`vka_mem.c` "File-backed pools", `vka_fileback.h`)

name: DM_MEM_FILEBACK_KINDS
meaning: `=shader` (default), `shader,texture` with `DM_MEM_FILEBACK=1`: `shader` = SHADER_CODE pools (the GPU never reads them on Android), `texture` = other pools of `DM_MEM_FILEBACK_MB` or more that are not physical, virtual or compressible (Ocarina of Time: ~2 GB of flash writes per area load, so only when chosen: the launcher's per-game Game settings › RAM saver sets `DM_MEM_FILEBACK=1 DM_MEM_FILEBACK_KINDS=shader,texture`)

name: DM_MEM_FILEBACK_MB
meaning: `=<MiB>` (64) with `DM_MEM_FILEBACK_KINDS` holding `texture`: smaller pools of that kind stay anonymous

name: DM_MEM_FOOT
meaning: `1` (Linux / Android, 0; Ocarina of Time 1 in its profile) `[mem] foot` lines with each `[mem] touched` line (`DM_MEM_TOUCHED_S`, which must be on): the guest's pages split into every memory pool (NVN flags, placed or not, the images over its storage by content: uploaded once, tracked, GPU content, levels left out), the heap and the alias region's mapped pages outside pools, the modules, the stack region and the rest below the alias region, each resident anonymous / resident shared (placed) / swapped / touched MiB and the change since the last line; the pools grouped by flags, placement and what the host still reads of them; one line a pool of `DM_MEM_FOOT_MB` touched; the 10 pools with the most swapped out; major and minor page faults since the last line (getrusage); the cost of the one pagemap pass it shares with the touched line (wall and CPU time, pagemap MiB read, placed MiB counted without a read); the pool table sized from the live pool count (a short one says "n of m pools"), NVN flags read for how many of NVN's live pools (`hle_svc.c` "Guest memory footprint", `dm/host/mem_foot.h`, `vka_mem.c` `dm_gfx_pool_foot`)

name: DM_MEM_FOOT_MB
meaning: `=<MiB>` (8; `0` none) pools with at least this much touched get a `[mem] foot pool` line each with `DM_MEM_FOOT=1` (32 at most, the largest first; the rest counted)

name: DM_MEM_TOUCHED_S
meaning: `=<seconds>` (Linux / Android, default 30, `0` off): a `[mem] touched` line that often and at exit: the guest heap, the alias region's mapped pages and the memory pools not placed yet, resident / shared / swapped / never touched from `/proc/self/pagemap` (mincore without it), plus zram's `mm_stat` when readable, the swap in use and the scan's cost (`hle_svc.c`, "Guest memory touched"; placed memory counted as resident shared without a read, "file" the shared or file pages outside it); `DM_MEM_FOOT=1` adds the footprint lines to it, from the same pagemap pass

name: DM_METAL_CAPTURE
meaning: `=1` makes `build_ipa.sh` produce a build that can write GPU frame captures (`MetalCaptureEnabled` in `Info.plist`), for `DM_GPU_CAPTURE`

name: DM_METAL_HUD
meaning: `1` shows Apple's Metal performance HUD over the game (frame rate, frame and GPU time, memory)

name: DM_MOTION
meaning: `0` ignores live motion: every six-axis sensor lies flat as before (a shake still plays), and neither controllers' motion sensors nor the phone's device motion are switched on (`hle_hid.c`, `motion_apple.h`, `DmGamepad.m`); the NSP script's `--no-motion` (`MOTION = False`) builds it in

name: DM_MOTION_ACC_SIGN
meaning: `-1` flips only GameController's acceleration, for a source that reports the specific force (+1 G up at rest) instead of the gravity direction (`motion_fusion.h`); phone and raw HID samples are already in the Switch frame

name: DM_MOTION_AXES
meaning: `=<map>` such as `x,-z,y`: maps Apple's controller axes to the Switch's, a signed permutation applied to acceleration and rotation alike, for a controller whose axes differ (default `x,y,z`; phone and raw HID samples are already in the Switch frame)

name: DM_MOTION_GAIN
meaning: `=<gain>`: how fast the orientation is pulled toward the measured gravity, in rad/s per unit error (default 0.5; `0` integrates the gyro alone)

name: DM_MOTION_HID
meaning: On the Mac, `0` disables the passive Switch Pro Controller HID motion fallback (`motion_pro_mac.h`); enabled by default when exactly one physical Pro and one GameController Pro can use the same player slot; usable GameController motion takes priority

name: DM_MOTION_LOG
meaning: `=1` logs player 1's mapped motion sample once a second per source (phone / GameController / controller HID; acceleration in G, gyro in revolutions/s), for checking the axes: flat and still reads acc 0 0 -1

name: DM_MOVIE_TRACE
meaning: When set, the movie decoder logs every call with its thread and decoder (by default the first 12 calls, then every 2^k-th)

name: DM_MSL_DIR
meaning: Parent folder of the shader libraries: NVN loads from `b-<chain version>/` beneath it, Vulkan from `vk/`, GL from `gl/`; the app and the Mac launcher set it

name: DM_NICK
meaning: The account nickname the game sees (default `Player`)

name: DM_NRO
meaning: `0` turns off loading of the NRO modules the game's NRR files register (on by default): every `nn::ro::LoadModule` then fails

name: DM_NUP_CACHE_MB
meaning: `=<MB>` sizes the cache of closed, decompressed `.nup` files (nup_image.c; default 128, `0` keeps nothing after close)

name: DM_NUP_DISK_MB
meaning: `=<MB>` (default 64; `0` none) a compressed `.nup` file of at least this size is decompressed into an unlinked temporary file and mapped, instead of whole into memory (nup_image.h)

name: DM_NVN_ALLOCPROF
meaning: `=1` charges Metal allocation growth to each replayed op type and function, and logs command allocator sizes and each new texture (serial, size, format, storage)

name: DM_NVN_API
meaning: `=<major>.<minor>` overrides the NVN API version `nvnDeviceGetInteger` reports (by default decided by the SDK version or the profile's `device_api`: 55.15 for SDK 11 and later, 53.313 before)

name: DM_NVN_BARRIER
meaning: How draw passes are ordered: `full` (default) waits for all earlier GPU work, `game` only for the previous pass's fragment stage unless the game set a barrier, `ab` alternates with the `DM_AB` phases

name: DM_NVN_BF_WANT
meaning: `=<file>`: appends the key of each fragment shader whose passes could not be merged for lack of a readable-tile version to that file, once per key

name: DM_NVN_BLIT_ORDER
meaning: `0` drops the barriers between dependent operations in the copy encoder, which reproduces the fountain's vertical stripes in Mario Wonder

name: DM_NVN_CAPTURE
meaning: `=<frame>:1:<path>` writes that frame (from its first submit to its present) to one file: pool bytes, registries, program keys, the textures whose content lives only in Metal, each submission's records with pointers relocatable, and the presented frame's SHA-256 and pixels; `dm/gfx/tests/nvn_replay` replays it ([development.md](development.md#frame-capture-and-replay))

name: DM_NVN_CBDUMP
meaning: `=<dir>`: saves each draw's whole uniform blocks as `F<frame>_p<pass>_st<stage>_cb<slot>_<address>.bin`, and the source bytes of buffer-to-3D-texture copies, with `DM_NVN_PASSDUMP`

name: DM_NVN_CBDUMP_KEY
meaning: `=<shader key>`: limits `DM_NVN_CBDUMP` to draws using that shader; for a vertex shader key also saves the draw's vertex streams and index buffer

name: DM_NVN_CBLOG
meaning: `=1` logs the command memory the game adds to command buffers (`AddCommandMemory`: the first 60, then every 500th) and the out-of-memory callbacks

name: DM_NVN_CLEARLOG
meaning: `=1` logs the first 40 colour clears drawn as a triangle (inside a pass, with a partial channel mask or a partial scissor)

name: DM_NVN_CMDSTAT
meaning: `=1` logs every 300 frames the command recording usage: bytes and records per frame, command memory segment sizes, out-of-memory callbacks, host segments, count and bytes per command type

name: DM_NVN_CPUPROF
meaning: 1 records CPU wall/time/instruction totals by renderer operation; off by default.

name: DM_NVN_CS_HOIST
meaning: `0` makes a compute dispatch between the draws of a pass end it (on by default: the dispatch runs ahead of the pass when that changes nothing the draws before it read)

name: DM_NVN_CUT
meaning: `=<draws>`: the replay commits its command buffer every that many draws, between passes (default 64; `0` one command buffer per submission, except the cut after a buffer-to-texture copy)

name: DM_NVN_DEFER
meaning: `0` turns off the deferred pass merging of the TBDR optimizations (which run only with `DM_NVN_TBDR=1`)

name: DM_NVN_DEFER_AB
meaning: `=1` keeps the deferred pass merging (with `DM_NVN_TBDR=1`) off until the second screenshot has been written, then turns it on, to compare the pictures with and without it

name: DM_NVN_DEPTHOVR
meaning: `=<fragment shader key prefix>,…`: those draws compare depth with `ALWAYS`; with `DM_NVN_HILITE`, tells "the depth test rejects every fragment" from "nothing rasterizes"

name: DM_NVN_DIRECT_UPLOAD
meaning: 0 disables bounded direct RGBA16F array uploads and keeps staged copies; on by default for supported non-sparse textures.

name: DM_NVN_DIRTYCHECK
meaning: `=1` fully hashes pool content on every use to find changes the dirty-page tracking missed

name: DM_NVN_DISPATCH_OWN
meaning: `=1` gives every compute dispatch a compute encoder of its own with full barriers, as before (by default dispatches share the copy encoder); `DM_NVN_PASSGPU` does the same

name: DM_NVN_DUAL_WANT
meaning: `=<file>`: appends the key of each pixel shader a pipeline blends with its output 1 as the second source, while it has no dual-source entry point, to that file, once per key (the profile's `dual_want.tsv`)

name: DM_NVN_ENC_LABEL
meaning: `=1` labels every render encoder `p<pass in frame> <width>x<height> <first 8 digits of the first draw's fragment key> d<draws>` for Instruments traces

name: DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD
meaning: `1` runs the replay's Metal encoding on a thread of its own while the submit thread goes on translating; on by default on iOS (`0` turns it off), off on macOS

name: DM_NVN_FAST_WAKE
meaning: `0` makes the game's `SyncWait`s wake on the commit feedback handler instead of the GPU's own signal of the fence (on by default)

name: DM_NVN_FB_SNAP
meaning: Draws that sample a colour attachment of their own render pass: unset, those that write it (or follow a write in the pass) read a snapshot, reused until the game's next barrier; `0` none; `all` a fresh snapshot for every draw that samples one (slow, diagnostic)

name: DM_NVN_FLUSH_FILL
meaning: `0` starts a new GPU texture in a CPU-writable pool as zeros; by default one whose storage the game flushed before its first use is filled from that storage once

name: DM_NVN_FRAMES
meaning: `=<N>` prints the NVN call table frame by frame for the first N frames (default 3)

name: DM_NVN_FUSE_CHECK
meaning: `=1` checks pass merging in the same frame: renders the merged passes again apart and logs the comparison of the attachments every time

name: DM_NVN_GEOMETRY_COLOR
meaning: full retains inactive geometry color attachments; default omits them only when attachment bounds and state prove equivalence.

name: DM_NVN_GEOMETRY_COMPUTE
meaning: split ends the geometry compute encoder after each stage for comparison; default combines compatible stages.

name: DM_NVN_GEOMETRY_CUT
meaning: 0 disables extra segment-cut checks at geometry encoder boundaries; default obeys the existing draw threshold and safety gates there.

name: DM_NVN_GEOMETRY_INDEX_CACHE
meaning: 0 disables exact-byte CPU primitive-map caching; default bounds it to 32 MiB and 4096 entries.

name: DM_NVN_GEOMETRY_PACK
meaning: legacy uses the serial block-prefix scan for comparison; default fuses small draws and scans large block totals in parallel.

name: DM_NVN_GEOMETRY_QUERY_RUN
meaning: 0 prevents geometry runs across samples-passed query reports/resets; default retains independent captures while queries replay at their raster positions.

name: DM_NVN_GEOMETRY_WAIT
meaning: always drains before indexed geometry preparation for comparison; default waits only for possible writes to CPU assembly inputs.

name: DM_NVN_GEO_HOIST
meaning: `0` draws each geometry draw's capture and kernel at its own place, ending the render pass; by default a run of lean geometry draws is prepared before the pass opens and only their rasters are drawn in it (`geo_run_walk`)

name: DM_NVN_GEO_LEAN
meaning: `0` draws passthrough geometry shaders through their full kernel and reader, as before; by default a lean kernel culls and the program's own vertex shader draws (`nvn_geometry.inc`)

name: DM_NVN_GEO_MESH
meaning: `0` draws passthrough geometry pairs that have a mesh library (`geo_mesh.tsv`) through the compute path; by default they are mesh draws in the render pass (`geo_mesh_draw`)

name: DM_NVN_GPUPROF
meaning: `=<f>`, `<f1>-<f2>` or `every:<n>`: logs the GPU start and duration of every encoder of those frames (`[gpuprof]` lines from Metal 4 counter heap timestamps)

name: DM_NVN_GPU_TS
meaning: `segment` or `submission`: what timestamp reports record (GPU start / end of the segment holding each report, or one time for the whole submission), instead of the profile's `gpu_timestamps`

name: DM_NVN_HILITE
meaning: `=<fragment shader key>,…`: those draws use a solid colour instead (magenta, green, cyan, yellow, blue, white in order), to tell wrong geometry from wrong shading

name: DM_NVN_INDLOG
meaning: `=<n>`: the first n indirect draws (and those of pass-dumped frames) log their arguments at encode and as the GPU left them once the submission completed, with the first indices

name: DM_NVN_IXCLOG
meaning: `=<n>` logs the first n indirect draw and dispatch conversions (record to arguments) once the GPU has run them

name: DM_NVN_KEYDUMP
meaning: `=<fs key>[:n[:every]]`: for up to n draws of that fragment shader (default 6), logs the pass dump binding lines plus vertex formats, vertex streams and uniform values; meant for devices

name: DM_NVN_LAZY_CLEAR
meaning: `0` makes clears with no draw after them open a pass of their own, as before; by default they wait to become the load action of the next pass on that target

name: DM_NVN_LOADPROBE
meaning: `=1`, `2` or `3`: attachments whose load is skipped are cleared to a sentinel colour (`3` NaN; `1` NaN for float formats) and the sentinel pixels left at pass end are counted (should be 0)

name: DM_NVN_LOG
meaning: `=1` logs the creation of NVN objects

name: DM_NVN_MAGSCAN
meaning: `=<fs key>[:every[:phase]]`: device self-check that reads each pass's colour attachments every `every` frames (default 30) and logs `[mag]` lines for solid magenta 16×16 blocks or non-finite pixels

name: DM_NVN_PASSDUMP
meaning: `=<f>`, `<f1>-<f2>` or `every:<n>`: logs every render pass of those frames (attachments, clears, shader keys, bindings, draw state, presents) for the `tbdr_*.py` tools

name: DM_NVN_PASSDUMP_ALL
meaning: `=1` makes `DM_NVN_PASSDUMP` record every draw and binding change, not only the first per pass and stage, including copies and inline uniform updates

name: DM_NVN_PASSGPU
meaning: `=<file>` writes the GPU time of each render and compute pass from stage-boundary timestamp counters (off under Metal 4); also gives each dispatch its own encoder

name: DM_NVN_PASSGPU_SERIAL
meaning: `=1` makes each encoder on the main command buffer wait until all earlier work has finished, so `DM_NVN_PASSGPU` times read each pass's exclusive time (totals read high)

name: DM_NVN_POOLS
meaning: set (any value): the pool census: per memory pool its flags and size, the bytes its buffers and textures cover, buffer-address queries, physical-mapping coverage and non-zero bytes, logged at presents 1, 60 and 300 (`hle_nvn.c`)

name: DM_NVN_PREDICT
meaning: `0` turns off the parallel precompile look-ahead: a pipeline miss compiles only the pipeline it needs

name: DM_NVN_PREFETCH
meaning: `0` turns off loading a program's shader libraries in the background when the game makes it (`nvnProgramSetShaders`); they load at its first draw instead

name: DM_NVN_PROF
meaning: `=1` wraps the implemented NVN functions in a timing wrapper and collects the time each takes during recording

name: DM_NVN_PROGTRACE
meaning: `=<vertex keys,...>` logs matching ProgramSetShaders calls and their guest backtraces

name: DM_NVN_REGLUM
meaning: `=x0,y0,x1,y1:<file>` (normalized coordinates): on every present records the present number, time, mean luminance and a grayscale thumbnail of that region, to check animation speed against frame rate

name: DM_NVN_RT_RANGE
meaning: `=1` (experimental, off by default; with `DM_NVN_TBDR=1`) keeps the pass open when the game sets the same colour and depth target again with a view that differs only in its level count

name: DM_NVN_RT_RANGE_CHECK
meaning: With `DM_NVN_RT_RANGE=1` and `DM_NVN_PASSDUMP`, renders a candidate pass both ways in the same frame and logs and writes the comparison (`CHECK_RESULTS.tsv`, `[RED]` on a difference)

name: DM_NVN_SHDUMP
meaning: `=<dir>` saves programs missing from the shader map as `<key>.ctl` (control section) and `<key>.code`, to find the files that hold them (the Mac, and the Vulkan replay on Android)

name: DM_NVN_SHDUMP_DIR
meaning: `=<dir>` (`shader_split.py`): the folder of `DM_NVN_SHDUMP` saves that the split adds to the shader map, after every file it reads (default `<version dir>/nvn_shdump`)

name: DM_NVN_SHMAP
meaning: The shader map (`shader_map.tsv`); `c1_full.tsv` and `pso_manifest.tsv` are taken from the same folder. Default: the game profile's folder on the Mac; the iOS app sets it

name: DM_NVN_SHOT
meaning: `=<frame>[,<frame>…]:<path>` saves the swapchain texture as an image at those frames (`%d` in the path = frame number)

name: DM_NVN_SHOT_OUT
meaning: `=<W>x<H>` makes `DM_NVN_SHOT` capture the picture as the present pass upscales it to that size, the crop included, instead of the raw swapchain texture

name: DM_NVN_SKIP_FS
meaning: `=<fragment key>[,…]` (up to 16) drops all draws of those fragment shaders, to measure their GPU cost or bisect a wrong draw; the picture is wrong

name: DM_NVN_SKIP_SMALL
meaning: `=<width>` drops all draws whose target width is at most that, to measure the cost of tiny render passes; the picture is wrong

name: DM_NVN_SLICE_MERGE
meaning: `0` keeps passes into other layers of one array or cube texture level apart (on by default: they run as one layered pass)

name: DM_NVN_SNAPRAW
meaning: `=1` makes `DM_NVN_TEXDUMP` also save each target's raw bytes, with a text header line, since converting an HDR target to an 8-bit image truncates

name: DM_NVN_STORAGE_FIRST_USE
meaning: `0` keeps a sampled block-compressed texture in a CPU-writable pool to the one-time fill instead of making it CPU-written when its storage holds data at first use (on by default; `tex_cpu_content`), to measure it

name: DM_NVN_T2T_FROM
meaning: `=<frame>`: `DM_NVN_T2T_TRACE` records copies only from that frame on (default 0)

name: DM_NVN_T2T_TRACE
meaning: `=<W>x<H>:<file>`: after each copy into an RGBA16F texture of that size, copies the result into a trace buffer on the GPU timeline; 240 entries are written to the file

name: DM_NVN_TBDR
meaning: `=1` turns on the replay's TBDR pass optimizations (store / load elision, pass merging, same-target continuation); off by default since bindless textures defeat their read inference

name: DM_NVN_TEXCPU
meaning: `=1` logs non-packaged (non-swizzled) textures in CPU-visible pools

name: DM_NVN_TEXDUMP
meaning: `=<frame>:<path>`, `size=<W>x<H>:<path>` or `layers=<n>:<path>`: saves every colour render target of that frame as PNG (`%d` = serial × 100 + layer × 10 + level)

name: DM_NVN_TEXINFO
meaning: `=<W>x<H>` logs storage and description of every texture of that size on first use, registration and initialization (pool, flags, packaged, non-zero bytes, swizzles)

name: DM_NVN_TEXRAW
meaning: `=<serial>,…` or `info` (the textures `DM_NVN_TEXINFO` picked out): saves those textures' raw bytes at the `DM_NVN_TEXDUMP` frame, with a text header line

name: DM_NVN_TEXSNAP
meaning: `=<in-frame pass index>,…`: with `DM_NVN_TEXDUMP`, copies those passes' colour attachments as they end and saves them with the end-of-frame dump

name: DM_NVN_TREG_ID
meaning: `=<n>` logs every registration of texture ID n: what it holds from then on, and the frame being recorded

name: DM_NVN_TSV
meaning: `=<path>` writes the per-frame NVN call table and timing rows (frame, metric, value) to a TSV, read by `scripts/bench.py`

name: DM_NVN_TSV_CALLS
meaning: `0` makes `DM_NVN_TSV` write only the timing rows, without the call counts (about two thirds of the file)

name: DM_NVN_UB
meaning: `="name=item,…;…"`: alternating measurement in one run; odd phases of `DM_NVN_UB_N` frames (default 180) take one category in turn (`@set:<global>=<value>` or dropped shader keys) and log present times

name: DM_NVN_UBP_CHECK
meaning: `=1` checks every uniform shadow made from memory: the pass ends, the updates land, the replay waits for the GPU and compares (a difference is a red line; slow)

name: DM_NVN_UB_COPY_THREAD
meaning: `0` copies uniform shadows of 512 bytes or more on the submit thread, as before (by default a worker copies them)

name: DM_NVN_UB_DEFER
meaning: `0` ends the render pass at every inline uniform update, as before; by default an update inside an open pass is deferred to the pass end and later draws read a shadow (off in TBDR mode)

name: DM_NVN_UB_LAZY
meaning: `=<n>`: the most deferred inline uniform updates kept across a render pass end (default 160); they land before the next copy, a conflicting draw or dispatch, or the submission end; `0` lands them at every pass end

name: DM_NVN_UB_N
meaning: `=<frames>`: the length of each phase of the same-process alternating measurement `DM_NVN_UB` (default 180, minimum 60)

name: DM_NVN_UB_PARTIAL
meaning: `0`: a uniform block the deferred updates cover only in part ends the pass, as before; by default its shadow starts from memory and takes the submission's queued updates (on by default)

name: DM_NVN_UDC_AB
meaning: `=1` starts with the DontCare store for unwritten attachments off and turns it on after the second screenshot, for an on/off picture comparison in one run

name: DM_NVN_UNWRITTEN_DC
meaning: `0` disables optional stores elided for loaded, unchanged attachments (on by default, independent of TBDR lookahead), for equivalence comparisons; mandatory image-write preservation stays active

name: DM_NVN_UPLOAD_REUSE
meaning: 0 keeps the original one-block upload-slot policy; default retains bounded demand-sized primary and overflow buffers after completion.

name: DM_NVN_VBUF_CACHE
meaning: `0` turns off the cache of resolved vertex stream addresses and vertex argument table writes across draws (on by default), for A/B runs

name: DM_NVN_VCONV_CHECK
meaning: `=1` scans the indices again at every reuse of a cached vertex conversion range (`vconv_range`) and reports differences

name: DM_NVN_VCONV_CPU
meaning: `=1` converts integer vertex inputs fed formats of another class on the CPU, as before, instead of through the shader's shadow inputs (`<key>_bv`)

name: DM_NVN_VCONV_RANGE
meaning: `0` / `1` overrides the profile's `vconv_range`: CPU vertex conversion only over the vertices each draw reads instead of the whole bound range

name: DM_NVN_VLOG
meaning: Set: logs each NVN memory pool as it is created (address, memory, size, flags) with a backtrace

name: DM_NVN_VSDUMP
meaning: Output file for post-vertex captures; used with DM_NVN_VSDUMP_KEY and the frame/count bounds

name: DM_NVN_VSDUMP_FROM
meaning: First presented frame eligible for a post-vertex capture (default 0)

name: DM_NVN_VSDUMP_KEY
meaning: Vertex key to capture, or `*` for all eligible vertex shaders; storage-writing shaders are excluded

name: DM_NVN_VSDUMP_MAX
meaning: Maximum post-vertex captures (default 1, or 256 for the wildcard key)

name: DM_NVN_WAITS
meaning: `=1` turns on the wait ledger: every place a host or game thread waits on the CPU for the GPU or the encode thread, counted per frame

name: DM_NVN_XV
meaning: `0` turns off the cross-submission attachment validity ledger, which skips write-backs of colour attachments cleared before their next use (on by default, only with `DM_NVN_TBDR` on)

name: DM_NVN_ZBLOCK
meaning: `=1` logs (`[zb]`) the all-zero blocks per level of each ASTC texture uploaded on the CPU (magenta when drawn); `=<folder>` also writes the raw storage of the first one per format and size

name: DM_NVN_ZSKIP
meaning: `0` turns off the zero-source skip, which drops a draw whose fragment shader is proven to write 0 over targets already 0 (on by default, only with `DM_NVN_TBDR` on)

name: DM_OE_SCRIPT
meaning: Scripted applet state changes at given seconds, `key=value@seconds,…` with keys `focus`, `opmode` and `bg` (`bg=1` / `bg=0` run the whole background round trip), e.g. `bg=1@20,bg=0@25`

name: DM_OODLE_HOST
meaning: The Mac host binary that `shader_split.py` runs in its Oodle tool mode to decode Trinity packs (`ONEPACK` files); set by the NSP script

name: DM_OODLE_JOB
meaning: `=<job file>`: the host runs the game's own Oodle decoder on every record of the job file right before `nnMain`, writes `<job file>.out` and exits (Unreal shader archives)

name: DM_OODLE_MODULES
meaning: The rewritten modules the Mac host's Oodle tool mode loads when `shader_split.py` decodes Trinity packs; set by the NSP script

name: DM_OODLE_SERVE
meaning: `=1`: the host answers decode requests on stdin / stdout with the game's own Oodle (or LZ5) decoder from the guest main thread before the SDK starts, until stdin ends

name: DM_OOT_MAX_RES
meaning: `1` (the rewriter's environment: `patch_nso.py`, or `scripts/pack_android.py`, which passes it on; default off) registers Ocarina of Time's max-resolution cut (`dm/games/0400486024DEC000/patches.py`): its dynamic-resolution update holds scale 1.0. A diagnostic, not a fix; the default rewrite has no cut

name: DM_OPMODE
meaning: The operation mode the game sees: `0` handheld, `1` console (default: the profile's `op_mode`, console unless set); read once at startup

name: DM_OVERLAY
meaning: `0` / `1` (Android) hides or shows the game overlay (build tag, frame rate, throttle dot) for a run, over the launcher's setting; read by the launcher from `env.txt`; the Vulkan replayer does not take it from a capture

name: DM_PACKER_COMMIT
meaning: `=<commit>` the packer commit `pack_android.py` writes as `pack.tsv`'s `packer` when the repository has no git (the phone: the app's `PackService` passes the commit it was built from); `shader_split.py`'s resume digest covers it. Default: `git rev-parse` of the repository, else `unknown`

name: DM_PAC_PROBE
meaning: `=1` logs, on each guest thread and nnMain's, what its pointer authentication keys make of one fixed pointer (`[pac] … IA … IB …`): tells whether threads share their keys (Android gives each its own IA key)

name: DM_PAD_DEADZONE
meaning: `=<r>` (Android, default 0.1) the gamepad sticks' radial dead zone, as a fraction of full deflection

name: DM_PAD_LABELLED
meaning: `1` / `0` (Android) maps a gamepad's face buttons by label instead of by position (the launcher's default: by position), for every pad

name: DM_PAD_MERGE
meaning: `=1` merges every controller into player 1, as before, instead of giving each controller a player of its own (Mac and iOS)

name: DM_PATCH_FRONT
meaning: `=<bytes>`: the size of the patch area right before the module base for a long text (`BIG_TEXT`); set only by the rewriter's own rerun with the size it needs

name: DM_PHONE_MOTION
meaning: On iOS, whether the phone's own device motion drives player 1's six-axis sensor: `auto` (default) while no controller supplies fresh motion, `1` phone only, `0` never; each source keeps its own orientation

name: DM_PREEMPT
meaning: `0` / `1` overrides the profile's `core_preempt`: also check already-runnable higher-priority peers on the caller's core after every thread SVC

name: DM_PRELOAD
meaning: Set: on the Mac, runs the host's early background loading (`dm_host_preload_start`) as the iOS app does, to exercise that path

name: DM_PRESENT_FIFO
meaning: `0` makes the display link take the newest queued frame each tick, as before; by default it shows frames in order, at most one tick behind

name: DM_PRESENT_HZ
meaning: `=<N>`: the frequency of presentation pacing (default 60); `0` means no frame limit and is for performance profiling only

name: DM_PRESENT_INTERVAL
meaning: `display` presents one frame per display-link tick whatever interval the game sets; `game` follows the game's present interval (default: the profile's `present_interval`)

name: DM_PRESENT_LATENCY
meaning: `=1` or `2`: overrides the display link's preferred frame latency for every screen and window mode; larger positive values use 2 (default 2 in variable-refresh fullscreen, 1 otherwise)

name: DM_PRESENT_LINK
meaning: Present pacing: `0` acquires the drawable itself, `1` (the default) presents on a 60 Hz display link, `2` uses a 120 Hz display link with a frame every other tick

name: DM_PRESENT_SNAP
meaning: `=<n>`: present snapshots, a ring of n host textures (2 to 4; `1` = 2) the presents are copied to so the game's swapchain texture is free at once; `0` off (default: the profile's `present_snap`)

name: DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE
meaning: `metalfx` scales a picture smaller than its rectangle on the screen through MetalFX's spatial scaler; `off` (the default) scales it bilinearly

name: DM_PROBE
meaning: `=module:offset,…` (Mac only): puts a `brk` at each guest address and on every hit prints the thread, registers, strings they point to and a backtrace, then runs the original instruction

name: DM_PROBE_ALL
meaning: Set: probe hits (`DM_PROBE`) also print x8–x18

name: DM_PROBE_DUMP
meaning: `=module:offset:length[:file]`: on the first hit of any probe, writes that range of guest memory to a file (default `run/<platform>/probe_dump.bin`)

name: DM_PROBE_FRAMES
meaning: Presented frame or inclusive `start-end` range in which guest probes print observations

name: DM_PROBE_HEAP
meaning: `=<name>,<start>,<size>,<free list>,<used list>`: hex offsets of the sead heap layout the probes' `!xN` heap walk uses (default Mario's `0,28,30,b0,c8`)

name: DM_PROBE_HEAPFRAME
meaning: `=<vtable offset in main>` (hex): the probes' heap walk treats heaps of that class as frame heaps (head +0xe0, tail +0xe8)

name: DM_PROBE_HEAPNAME
meaning: `=<text>`: the probes' `!xN` heap walk reports only hits on heaps whose name contains the text

name: DM_PROBE_HEAPRAW
meaning: Set: the probes' heap walk also prints the heap object's first 0x130 bytes

name: DM_PROBE_HEAPWORDS
meaning: Set: the probes' heap walk also prints each used block's first two words

name: DM_PROBE_LIMIT
meaning: Maximum printed hits per guest probe; 0 or absent leaves the count unlimited

name: DM_PROBE_POLL
meaning: `=<address>[+<length>]` (hex, 4 bytes by default, up to 8): a host thread spins on the bytes and on each change snapshots every thread's pc, lr and frames, for writes the watch misses

name: DM_PROBE_WATCH
meaning: `=<address>[+<length>]` (hex, 8 bytes by default): write-protects that host page and reports who writes these bytes, without a debugger

name: DM_PROBE_X2
meaning: `=<bytes>` (hex): probe hits also dump that many bytes of the memory x2 points to

name: DM_PROGRAM_ID
meaning: `=<hex>`: the program ID the host reports from `svcGetInfo(ProgramId)` (default: the profile's `program_id`)

name: DM_PSO_ARCHIVE
meaning: The folder of the per-game Metal 4 pipeline archive of pipeline bases (default `pso_archive/` beside `pso_user.tsv`); `off` keeps no archive

name: DM_PSO_BUNDLE
meaning: The pipeline archive made offline (`<GPU architecture>.mtl4a`, `prebuilt.tsv`), read only; the iOS app and Mac launcher set it to their `pso/` folder; `off` ignores it

name: DM_PSO_GPUS
meaning: `build_ipa.sh`: the GPU architectures, comma-separated, to build the offline pipeline archive for (`none` builds none); unset, a profile with `pso_mtl4 on` gets its `pso_gpu` list or `g18p` when absent; profiles with `pso_mtl4 off` get none

name: DM_PSO_HYBRID
meaning: `0`: a draw whose pipeline is not built yet waits for it instead of drawing with its shader pair's pulling pipeline meanwhile (on by default with the Metal 4 path)

name: DM_PSO_IOS_MIN
meaning: `build_ipa.sh`: the minimum iOS version of the offline pipeline archives (default the SDK's major version); a device of another major version cannot open them and builds the bases itself

name: DM_PSO_MANIFEST
meaning: The prewarm manifest to use instead of the profile's `pso_manifest.tsv`; `off` turns the prewarm off

name: DM_PSO_MTL4
meaning: `0` builds render pipelines through the `MTLDevice` with no bases and no archive; `1` uses MTL4Compiler with the archive, hybrid pipelines and prebuild (default on on the Mac, the profile's `pso_mtl4` on iOS)

name: DM_PSO_PAIRS
meaning: The prebuild's second shader pair table (default: `pso_pairs.tsv` beside the shader map)

name: DM_PSO_PREBUILD
meaning: `0` turns off the prebuild of every known shader pair's pulling base into the pipeline archive (on by default); `tool` runs the prebuild alone on the Mac and exits

name: DM_PSO_PREBUILD_DEPTH
meaning: `zero`: the prebuild tool (`DM_PSO_PREBUILD=tool`) builds bases for the near = 0 depth mode; the NSP script sets it from the profile's `depth_mode`

name: DM_PSO_PREBUILD_THREADS
meaning: `=<n>`: the workers of the prebuild tool (`DM_PSO_PREBUILD=tool`; default: the performance cores less one)

name: DM_PSO_PREPARE
meaning: `0` runs the prewarm in the background while the game starts, as without a window; `1` makes the first submission wait for the prewarm lists also without a window

name: DM_PSO_PREPARE_THREADS
meaning: `=<n>`: the workers of the prepare step that builds the prewarm lists before the first frame (default: the device's active cores)

name: DM_PSO_PULL_ALL
meaning: `=1`: every draw that has a pulling pipeline draws with it, never with the pipeline for its vertex layout

name: DM_PSO_RECORD
meaning: `=<file>`: appends the shaders and pipelines used in the run to that file, for re-recording the prewarm manifest

name: DM_PSO_USER
meaning: The per-device list of shaders and pipelines built on the spot (default: `pso_user.tsv` in the parent of `DM_SAVE`)

name: DM_PSO_WAITLOG
meaning: `=1` logs each draw that waited more than 20 ms for its pipeline, with its shader pair and why no stand-in served it

name: DM_QOS_EDGES
meaning: `=e1,e2`: the Switch priority edges of `DM_QOS_MAP` (default `44,59`)

name: DM_QOS_MAP
meaning: `=1` maps guest thread priority to QoS class: ≤ 44 user-interactive, 45–59 user-initiated, the rest utility (off by default: every guest thread runs user-interactive)

name: DM_REC
meaning: `=<file>`: writes player 1's physical input (keyboard, mouse touches, controllers; never `DM_KEYS` / `DM_CTL`) to the file as `DM_KEYS` steps in presented frames, for replaying a run (`DM_KEYS=@<file>`)

name: DM_REGIONS
meaning: `=<file>` writes the table of the SDK's address regions every 2 s (alias offset, size, where the request returns to in the game, bytes mapped, the part opened, the SDK offset the request came through; `hle_svc.c` "Address regions"); the NSP script's address region check sets it

name: DM_RENDER_SCALE
meaning: `0.5` to `1.0`: fixes the game's 3D views at that fraction of their size and turns its dynamic resolution off, for builds with a render scale stub; `1.0` (the default) keeps it

name: DM_RESOURCE_AOC
meaning: The add-on content folder the iOS build copies into the app's `aoc/` (empty for none); written by `gen_resources.py`, read by `stage_resources.sh`

name: DM_RESOURCE_BUILD
meaning: Package version (for example `v327680`), written to `Gen/resources.env` by `gen_resources.py`; with `DM_COPY_ROMFS=NO` the copy phase puts it in the `build=` field of the app's `romfs.id`

name: DM_RESOURCE_CHAIN_H
meaning: Path of `dm/gfx/nvn/dmsh_chain.h`, written to `Gen/resources.env` by `build_ipa.sh`; the Xcode copy phase (`stage_resources.sh`) stops when the prepared shaders are not of its chain version

name: DM_RESOURCE_MARKER
meaning: A file under the RomFS, written to `Gen/resources.env` by `build_ipa.sh`, that the Xcode copy phase (`stage_resources.sh`) checks for before copying the game files

name: DM_RESOURCE_MSLDIR
meaning: Name of the shader library folder (`b-<chain>`), written to `Gen/resources.env` by `build_ipa.sh`; the Xcode copy phase copies the shaders to `msl/<name>` in the app

name: DM_RESOURCE_PSO
meaning: Folder of the offline Metal pipeline archive (empty for none), written to `Gen/resources.env` by `build_ipa.sh`; the Xcode copy phase copies it to `<App>/pso`

name: DM_RESOURCE_ROMFS
meaning: RomFS folder, written to `Gen/resources.env` by `build_ipa.sh`; the Xcode copy phase (`stage_resources.sh`) copies it into the app's `romfs`

name: DM_RESOURCE_SHADERS
meaning: iOS shader library folder, written to `Gen/resources.env` by `build_ipa.sh`; the Xcode copy phase (`stage_resources.sh`) copies it into the app's `msl/b-<chain>`

name: DM_RESOURCE_TITLE
meaning: Game profile title ID, written to `Gen/resources.env` by `gen_resources.py`; with `DM_COPY_ROMFS=NO` the copy phase puts it in the `title=` field of the app's `romfs.id`

name: DM_RESOURCE_VERSION
meaning: Display version, written to `Gen/resources.env` by `gen_resources.py`; with `DM_COPY_ROMFS=NO` the copy phase puts it in the `version=` field of the app's `romfs.id`

name: DM_RES_CHECK
meaning: `=1` prints the first 40 textures or buffers a shader reaches through its argument block that are not in the residency set (textures attributed to their parent allocation)

name: DM_REWRITE_J
meaning: `=<positive integer>`: worker processes per module for `patch_nso.py`'s x18 scan and spin wait search; `=1` runs serially. Default: one per core directly, an automatic per-module budget in the NSP script. An explicit value overrides that budget

name: DM_ROMFS
meaning: The game's RomFS folder, mounted read-only as `rom` (default `$DM_ROOT/romfs`); the Mac launcher, the iOS app and the NSP script set it

name: DM_ROMFS_OVERLAY
meaning: `=<dir>[:<dir>…]`: RomFS reads look in these folders first, in order, and fall back to `DM_ROMFS` (for a modified copy of some files)

name: DM_ROOT
meaning: Workspace root (default `~/dm-work`): the host's and tools' default paths (RomFS, temporary storage, shader libraries under `build/cache/metal_shader_cache`, probe dumps) are under it

name: DM_RT
meaning: `0` leaves the thread that acquires the window on its QoS only, with no Mach time-constraint policy declaring the frame deadline (on by default; for power A/B)

name: DM_RT_COMP
meaning: `=<ms>` fixes the computation the present thread's time-constraint policy declares; default `auto` re-declares it every 120 frames from that thread's per-frame CPU time (p90 and peak)

name: DM_RUMBLE
meaning: `0` turns game rumble off (on by default); launcher setting

name: DM_RUMBLE_GAIN
meaning: `=0..3` scales the rumble strength (default 1, `0` is silent); launcher setting

name: DM_RUMBLE_LOG
meaning: `=1` logs the game's vibration handle requests and, once a second, the values it sent, how many had no routed output and the peak amplitude

name: DM_RUMBLE_MIN
meaning: `=0..0.9`: controller rumble levels below it stay silent and the rest is stretched over the full range (default 0; the phone is unaffected); for games whose quiet HD rumble texture keeps rotating motors running (Mario Kart 8 Deluxe: 0.45); launcher setting

name: DM_SAVE
meaning: This run's save folder (must be set); the device save is `<DM_SAVE>_device`, and `pso_user.tsv` goes in its parent folder; the Mac launcher, the iOS app and the NSP script set it

name: DM_SAVED_CHOICES
meaning: `0` ignores the player's saved choices (launcher.<VAR> in the app's preferences) and leaves them saved; the Mac launcher and the iOS settings screen

name: DM_SAVE_SYNC
meaning: Cloud saves: the folder whose `<title ID>/save.dmsync` the save is synced through, `icloud` for iCloud Drive/nxnative Saves (the Mac); `0` or unset, off. The Mac launcher sets the folder chosen in its settings window's Cloud saves, the iPhone app the one picked in its launcher (dm/host/save_sync.h)

name: DM_SCHEME_NAME
meaning: Set by `build_ipa.sh` itself for xcodegen's `project.yml`: the Xcode scheme name, `DmIOS`, or `<display name> (<title ID>)` for a project prepared with `--prepare-xcode`

name: DM_SCREEN_MATCH
meaning: `0` keeps the screen's refresh rate in fullscreen; by default a Mac screen whose rate is not a multiple of the game's frame rate switches to one that is (144 → 120 Hz)

name: DM_SF_TRACE
meaning: `=1` logs every request on the game's own HIPC client sessions that the host answers (`hle_sf.c`)

name: DM_SHAKE_G
meaning: `=<G>`: on iOS, the acceleration beyond gravity above which a flick of the phone shakes the controller's six-axis sensor (default 1.5)

name: DM_SHARED_FONT
meaning: Font file served for every shared-font type except the Nintendo extension (default `$DM_FONT_DIR/standard.ttf`, then macOS's Arial Unicode)

name: DM_SHARED_FONT_EXT
meaning: Font file served for shared-font type 5, the Nintendo extension with the button icons (default `$DM_FONT_DIR/nintendo_ext.ttf`, made by `make_ext_font.py`)

name: DM_SHOW_FPS
meaning: `1` shows the frame-rate counter on the iPhone (frames put on screen per second, top left); at IPA build it sets `DMShowFPS` in `Info.plist`, which `Documents/env.txt` overrides

name: DM_SKIP
meaning: Intro skip, a debug aid for test runs (off by default; android/TESTING.md, Intro skip): `1` arms it, so holding Minus+Plus for 1 s on player 1 turns it on (and again off); `auto` also turns it on at start. While on, it presses `DM_SKIP_KEYS` every few frames, ends movies early and turns itself off at gameplay (`DM_SKIP_UNTIL`); the `DM_CTL` line `skip on|off|toggle` works without it

name: DM_SKIP_EVERY
meaning: `=<frames>`: the intro skip presses its keys for 3 presented frames in every that many (default 12, 4 at least)

name: DM_SKIP_KEYS
meaning: `=<key>[+key],…`: what the intro skip presses, an entry a press in turn (default `A`; `DM_KEYS` key names)

name: DM_SKIP_MAX
meaning: `=<seconds>`: the intro skip turns itself off after that long (default 300; 0 = never)

name: DM_SKIP_MOVIES
meaning: `0` keeps the intro skip from ending movies (`nn::codec` and `nn::movie` streams end after their first picture while it is on)

name: DM_SKIP_UNTIL
meaning: `=<draws> [seconds]`: the intro skip turns itself off that many seconds after 5 presented frames in a row with that many draws or more (default the profile's `skip_until_draws`; none: only `DM_SKIP_MAX` or by hand)

name: DM_SLOWFRAME
meaning: `=1` writes the per-frame timing breakdown to the log only for dropped frames (kept in a ring of the last 16 frames, judged 8 frames late)

name: DM_SPIN
meaning: `0` makes the rewriter's spin gate return at once, so guest poll loops spin with no sleep; the gate stays (on by default)

name: DM_SPIN_LIST
meaning: `=1` makes `patch_nso.py` print every guest poll loop it found and sends through a spin gate

name: DM_SPIN_POLL
meaning: `=<µs>`: how long a spin-gate wait polls before it sleeps with the yield back-off (default 2000; `0` yields on every pass)

name: DM_SPLIT_RESUME
meaning: `=<dir>` (the phone's split: `PackService`) `shader_split.py` keeps each RomFS file's scan results there and a rerun takes those whose inputs, tools and profile digest still match, so a stopped split resumes per file; unset: no kept results (the Mac's split)

name: DM_SVC
meaning: `=1` logs memory SVCs (`SetHeapSize`, `MapMemory`, `Map`/`UnmapPhysicalMemory`) with their addresses and sizes

name: DM_SYMCHECK
meaning: `=1` checks every hashed module symbol lookup against a linear search and logs a red line for each mismatch

name: DM_TBUF_ALIGN
meaning: `=<bytes>` uses that value as the linear-texture alignment for buffer textures when it is larger than the device's `minimumLinearTextureAlignmentForPixelFormat`: a Mac can then reproduce a phone's larger alignment (a 64-byte one fails the buffers a device with 64 bytes cannot view), to check `tbuf_as_2d`'s aligned-row copy

name: DM_TEAM_ID
meaning: Apple team ID for the per-game Xcode project, used when `--team-id` / `TEAM_ID` is not given; `build_ipa.sh` uses the placeholder `0000000000` (unsigned) when unset

name: DM_TEMP
meaning: Temporary storage folder (default `$DM_ROOT/run/platform/temp`); stand-in system data goes in `<DM_TEMP>_sysdata`; the Mac launcher, the iOS app and the NSP script set it

name: DM_TEST_ARCHIVE_CONSTANTS
meaning: Use optional function constants in the synthetic pipeline archive restart fixture

name: DM_TEST_ARCHIVE_MIXED
meaning: Mix a newly compiled shader function with compacted bases in the archive restart fixture

name: DM_TEST_BORDER
meaning: Path to the native t_border executable that test_dmsh_border.py runs a rewritten shader through on the GPU (`make check_t_border` sets it)

name: DM_TEST_BUILD
meaning: Build folder of `dm/host/tests` whose `t_svc_memory` `test_memory_profile.py` runs (default `build`; `make asan` sets `build/asan`)

name: DM_TEST_FS_FAIL
meaning: `=write:<n>[:<errno>]` makes the nth save write fail with that errno (default ENOSPC), which refuses the save transaction's commit

name: DM_TEST_FS_FAILAT
meaning: `=<point>[:<count>][,…]` makes steps of the save transaction (`mountclone`, `reclone`, `guestname`, `renameback`) fail with ENOSPC

name: DM_TEST_GEOMETRY
meaning: Path of the native `t_geometry` executable; `test_dmsh_geometry.py` runs its native geometry emitter checks only when it is set

name: DM_TEST_GEOMETRY_PRIMITIVE_ID
meaning: Path to the native t_geometry_primitive_id replay executable used by test_dmsh_geometry.py with DMSH_TEST_GPU=1.

name: DM_TEST_KEYRACE
meaning: `=<n>` creates up to n (at most 512) pthread keys on a thread of its own while the host starts up

name: DM_TEST_KILL_AT
meaning: `=write:<n>` exits the process (`_exit(9)`) at the nth save write, imitating a kill mid-write

name: DM_TEST_LEAK_GPU
meaning: `=1` allocates and keeps a 1 MB shared Metal buffer every 100 ticks: a GPU memory leak on demand

name: DM_TEST_LINK_STALL
meaning: `=<start s>,<duration s>`: counting from the first present, pauses the display link at that point for that long, to check the present fallback

name: DM_TEST_NO_METAL4
meaning: `=1` treats the GPU as one without Metal 4, as on a virtual Mac: the NVN layer starts only its classic part and drops every present

name: DM_TEST_PRESENT_LAG
meaning: `=<every n>,<ms>[,<in a row>][;…]` sleeps that long before every nth present (and the ones after it in the run): a slow frame on demand

name: DM_TEST_SWKBD_HOLD_MS
meaning: `=<ms>` (with `DM_KBD`) keeps the system keyboard up that long before `DM_KBD`'s text is returned, as a player typing would

name: DM_TEST_SWKBD_LAG_MS
meaning: `=<ms>` sleeps that long between the keyboard handing back its text and the game's thread getting the result, to check that auto-accept does not act early

name: DM_TEST_TRANSFORM_FEEDBACK
meaning: Path to the native t_transform_feedback executable used by the Python feedback tests

name: DM_TEST_UP_LEAK
meaning: `=1` keeps the old upload staging block instead of retiring it, as before the fix, to measure the leak

name: DM_TEST_UP_LOST
meaning: `=<batch index>` treats that batch of uploads as dropped, to exercise the re-upload path

name: DM_THERMAL_CAP
meaning: `0` turns off the thermal cap, which holds the frame step at 30 fps while iOS reports a serious or critical thermal state (on by default)

name: DM_THR
meaning: `=1` logs each SVC (except `SleepThread`) with its first four arguments, and each `CreateThread` with entry, stack, priority and core

name: DM_THRCPU
meaning: `=<tsv path>[,<seconds>]` writes each thread's CPU time (100% = one core) and the total every interval (default 10 s); on iOS a relative path is under `Documents`

name: DM_TOUCH_HAPTICS
meaning: `0` turns off the light haptic tap when a touch control is pressed (on by default); launcher setting

name: DM_TOUCH_LOG
meaning: `=1` logs each touch-screen read with touch points (sample, finger, position, attributes) and each gesture entry, up to 500 lines

name: DM_UDC_SELFTEST
meaning: `=1` runs a start-up check of DontCare load and store on private depth-stencil and RGBA8 textures (clear, Load + DontCare, read back) and logs one result line

name: DM_UE_SHADERS
meaning: Folder of the Unreal shader code archives decoded by `uepak.py`, for `shader_split.py` (default `ue_shaders` beside the RomFS); needed when the RomFS has Unreal paks

name: DM_UE_TEXTURE_POOL
meaning: Megabytes Unreal's texture streaming pool (`r.Streaming.PoolSize`) is raised to, overriding the profile's `ue_texture_pool`; `0` keeps the game's own pool. On iOS only this switch turns it on (`Documents/env.txt`)

name: DM_VK_ADPF
meaning: `0` (Android, restart, on) no ADPF performance hint session (`APerformanceHint`, `vka_perf.c`): the replay reports no work durations to the system

name: DM_VK_ADPF_GPU
meaning: `0` (Android, live, 1) ADPF work duration reports leave out the frame's GPU time (with `1` they carry it when the platform has `AWorkDuration`, and then the `DM_VK_ADPF_SPAN` span)

name: DM_VK_ADPF_PIPELINE
meaning: `0` (Android, restart, default 1) the ADPF session is made plainly instead of as part of the graphics pipeline (`ASessionCreationConfig_setGraphicsPipeline`, API 36; a session the platform refuses as one is made plainly)

name: DM_VK_ADPF_SPAN
meaning:
`=

` (Android, live; unset: 100 when ADPF is the GPU clock floor, `DM_VK_GPU_FLOOR_ADPF`, else 0): ADPF reports each frame's span (recording start to the GPU end of its last submission) against p % of the game's shortest period (`DM_VK_GPU_FLOOR_PERIOD`) instead of the period against the period; `0` the old reports

name: DM_VK_AFF_ALL
meaning: `=<mask>` (Android, live, 0 = untouched) sets the CPU affinity of every thread of the process to that CPU bit mask when the value changes (`sched_setaffinity`); logs the thread count

name: DM_VK_AFF_REPLAY
meaning: `=<mask>` (Android, live, 0 = untouched) sets the replay worker thread's CPU affinity to that CPU bit mask when the value changes

name: DM_VK_BAR_KEEP
meaning: `1` (Android, live, off): a game barrier inside an open draw pass is taken inside the pass when no draw of the pass wrote memory (later draws that write memory, read the texture pool or sample an attachment of the pass end it); `0` ends the pass at every barrier. Off until phone-checked

name: DM_VK_BIGIMG_MB
meaning: `=<MiB>` (Android, default 64) logs a `large image:` line (texture serial, size, format, flags, pool) for each image whose memory is at least that size, the first 32; for those images also their first GPU write (frame and site), the other textures found over their storage, and a `ctl: large images the GPU has not written` line with the stats (the largest 8, with the draws that sampled them and what lies over their storage)

name: DM_VK_CAPTURE
meaning: `=<dir>` (Mac) writes every SPIR-V module the game creates to `<dir>/<key>.spv`; the NSP script's Vulkan shader capture stage sets it

name: DM_VK_CHUNK
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, live: the next submission, default 600; `0` one part) a long submission goes to the queue in parts: after n draws of the part in progress it is ended and submitted at the next pass boundary, so the GPU starts while the rest is recorded

name: DM_VK_CHUNK_PASS
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, live, default 600; `0` off) a part is also ended and submitted inside an open pass after n draws, when the pass can be split there ([rendering.md](reference/rendering.md#gpu-end-held-back-by-recording-and-a-clocked-down-gpu-on-the-vulkan-replay))

name: DM_VK_CS_SHARED_OVER
meaning: `1` (Android, live, off) makes compute programs whose shared memory exceeds the device's `maxComputeSharedMemorySize` anyway (by default they are not made and their dispatches are skipped); an A/B

name: DM_VK_DEPTH_ALIAS
meaning: `0` (Android, live: lookups from then on, 1) a single-channel colour texture over a depth texture's storage of the same shape and encoding (R32F over DEPTH32F, R16 over DEPTH16) gets an image of its own, as before (zeros); on, its sampled lookups share the depth image through a depth-aspect view, and a write lookup gives it an image of its own again (`vka_tex.c` "Colour textures over a depth image") ([rendering.md](reference/rendering.md))

name: DM_VK_DISPATCH_LOG
meaning: `1` (Android, live: the next frame) logs one line per dispatch (its index in the frame, shader key, groups, workgroup size, shared memory, flags); `2` also each texture and image it binds, with the texture serial (for `nxctl.sh texshot`), and the compute storage slots the game set (address, size, whether placed, what holds the first and last byte)

name: DM_VK_DISPATCH_SKIP
meaning: `=<from>[,<to>]` (Android, live) dispatches from..to of each frame (by `DM_VK_DISPATCH_LOG`'s index; default to the end) are recorded without their `vkCmdDispatch`, to find the one that writes a wrong picture

name: DM_VK_DONE_LAST
meaning: `1` (Android, live, off) the completion thread waits for the last fence handed to the queue instead of the next one, as before (it held earlier fences back until all queued work had run); for A/B runs

name: DM_VK_DRAW
meaning: `0` / `1` (Android, live) turns draws and dispatches off or on (their records are skipped; events, counters and fences still signal); default on with placed guest memory, off without it

name: DM_VK_DRAWDUMP_FS
meaning: `=<fragment shader key>` (Android, live: each time the switch is set, once) the next draw with that fragment shader logs every buffer its fragment stage binds (guest address and size against the walk's, the descriptor's offset and range, the c0 storage table words) and writes their first 4 KiB to `<files>/drawdump/ld<n>_<key>_<c3|s0|...>.bin`; for Ocarina of Time's Model.Product.110 light loop (keys verified from the SPIR-V in `vka_draw.c`) also the cluster grid, the cap `c6[113].x`, the per-cluster light counts (min / median / p90 / p99 / max, above the cap, mean loop trip; `..._counts.bin`) and how far the lists and light records reach against the bound sizes and descriptors

name: DM_VK_DRAW_DUMP
meaning: `=<vertex shader key>:<folder>[:<draws>]` (Android) writes the guest bytes the first draws (default 4) of that vertex shader read, as the CPU sees them at recording, into the folder: each buffer binding of every stage with 4 KB around it, each driver segment as the replay fills it, the vertex streams and the index buffer, and `dd.txt` with the draws' arguments and the storage descriptors' offsets (to run the draw's shader off the phone)

name: DM_VK_DRAW_LOG
meaning: `1` (Android, live) logs each texture and image every draw binds, per stage, with its texture serial (for `nxctl.sh texshot`): which texture a UI's text or a wrong surface samples; each buffer it binds with its first words, the targets of each pass a draw opens, each vertex input (format, stride, per vertex / per instance, first values) and the draw's state (mask, blend, viewport, scissor, culling, depth / stencil, primitive, base instance, module variant, alpha test, alpha to coverage); a draw dropped for an empty scissor says so

name: DM_VK_DRIVER
meaning: `=<folder>` or `=<file>.so` (Android, restart) a custom Vulkan driver (a folder with a `meta.json` naming its library, loaded through libadrenotools from the app's private files); unset or `system`: the system driver; the launcher's GPU driver setting sets it, a line in `env.txt` wins

name: DM_VK_DRV_MEMO
meaning: (Android, live, on) a driver segment (c0, c2, the push bank) or the gmem table whose bytes equal the last draw's binds the same scratch span again instead of a fresh fill per draw; `0` fills one per draw

name: DM_VK_DYN_FILTER
meaning: `0` / `2` (Android, live: the next submission, default 1) `1` skips dynamic state and pipeline binds equal to the last ones; `0` sets them at every draw; `2` sets them again at each pass (to bisect)

name: DM_VK_ENC
meaning: `0` (Android, live: the next submission, default 1) the replay makes its `vkCmd*` calls itself instead of through the command encoder thread (`vka_enc.c`, `vk-enc`); also off while `DM_VK_GPUPROF` times a frame or `DM_VK_NANSCAN` is on

name: DM_VK_ENC_BATCH
meaning: `=<bytes>` (Android, live, 4096; at most 1 MB) the replay feeds the command encoder thread in batches of that many bytes instead of waking it for each call; `0` each call

name: DM_VK_EVICT
meaning: `0` (Android, live, 1) keeps every image until its last texture object is finalized, as before; on, once a second an image that no lookup found for `DM_VK_EVICT_S` seconds, that no registered texture ID names and that nothing else holds is destroyed (not on a device without null descriptors) with its memory after the submission being recorded, and made again from its storage if a serial of it is used again; an image the GPU wrote goes only once a newer image (GPU-written, or filled from the storage under `DM_VK_EVICT_OVER`) lies over its storage; under `DM_VK_EVICT_OVER` such a newer image also lets a named image go, its IDs deferred again; `2` also lets a named image go that the GPU never wrote, no image registration names, and no scanned storage buffer named for `DM_VK_EVICT_S` (neither as a handle nor by the low 20 bits; only while lazy images hold, at most 64 MiB a second, a serial made again after it pinned), its IDs deferred again (`vka_tex.c` "Image eviction"; `image eviction:` and `image eviction kept:` lines, and `evicted` in the ctl stats) ([memory.md](reference/memory.md))

name: DM_VK_EVICT_OVER
meaning: `0` (Android, live, 1) the overlap rule of `DM_VK_EVICT` counts only newer GPU-written images, as before; on, a newer image filled from the storage counts too, and an idle image a registered texture ID names goes when such a newer image lies over its storage, unless an image registration names it or a scanned storage buffer named its ID in the handle form within `DM_VK_EVICT_S` (only while lazy images hold): its IDs go back to the deferred state and a pool-reading draw that names one again remakes it from the storage; a serial made again after that is pinned (`vka_tex.c` "Image eviction") ([memory.md](reference/memory.md))

name: DM_VK_EVICT_S
meaning: `=<seconds>` (Android, live, 10; at least 2) how long `DM_VK_EVICT` waits after an image's last lookup before it may let the image go, in seconds of submitting (at most one second counted a submission)

name: DM_VK_FG
meaning: not read as a switch: a prefix in the Vulkan replayer's list of the live run's settings it does not take from a capture (`vka_replay.c`), which covers `DM_VK_FG_REFRESH_CAP`

name: DM_VK_FG_REFRESH_CAP
meaning: (Android, live, 1) frame generation makes no more images per game frame than the panel's refreshes in the game's period (display timing): on a 60 Hz panel a 60 fps game gets none instead of being held at 30 fps by FIFO; `0` generates the multiplier's count whatever the panel runs at (a driver whose display timing reports a refresh the panel does not run at)

name: DM_VK_FOUT_RETYPE
meaning: `=0` (Android): a pixel shader's float output into a UINT / SINT attachment is not retyped (`vka_spv_fout_retype`); that target is not written, the earlier behaviour; default on

name: DM_VK_FRAME_RATE
