meaning: `0` (Android, live, 1) the window is not given the game's frame rate (`ANativeWindow_setFrameRate`, held by `DM_VK_FRAME_RATE_HOLD`); the panel's rate is left to the system

name: DM_VK_FRAME_RATE_HOLD
meaning: `=<ms>` (Android, live, 5000) the window's frame rate is the highest the game used in that time: up at once, down only after the lower rate has held that long (DKB's 60 <-> 30 switches sent the LTPO panel to 30 Hz and back, a hitch each); `0` follows every change

name: DM_VK_FSR
meaning: `1` (Android, live, off) the picture is scaled up to the window with AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 1 (EASU, then RCAS sharpening; `vka_present.c`, `dm/third_party/fidelityfx-fsr1`) instead of the bilinear blit, when it is smaller than the window, pre-rotated or not; turned on during a run, the next swapchain gets the attachment views it needs

name: DM_VK_FSR_SHARP
meaning: `=<stops>` (Android, live, 0.25) `DM_VK_FSR`'s RCAS sharpening in stops: 0 is the strongest, each stop halves it (AMD's scale, `FsrRcasCon`)

name: DM_VK_GMEM_PIDX_BUFS
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, read at each new generation, 4; at most 8; a buffer once made stays for the process) buffers the raw global memory page index (`vka_draw.c` gmem_pidx) is kept in, each the pool table plus one 8-byte record per 4 KiB page of the window (~20.7 MiB each for Ocarina of Time): a new table generation takes one the GPU is done with, else waits for the oldest (`waits for a buffer` in the `[reach]` line); Ocarina of Time's profile sets 2

name: DM_VK_GMEM_PIDX_MB
meaning: `=<MiB>` (Android, live, 256) at most that many MiB of page index records (with the device's maxStorageBufferRange); table entries past that window go to the sink (`table entries left out` in the `[reach]` line)

name: DM_VK_GMEM_SINK_FILL
meaning: `=<byte>` (Android, read once at the sink's creation, `0xA5`) the byte raw global memory's sink is filled with (what a shader's load of an address in no pool, or past the table's 4095 entries, reads); `0xFF` makes such loads NaN, so `DM_VK_NANSCAN` shows where they land; the store check compares against it, and each find counts in the `[reach]` line

name: DM_VK_GPL
meaning: `0` (Android, restart, on where the device has them with fast linking) graphics pipeline libraries off: a pipeline the cache lacks is made whole instead of linked from stage libraries with the optimized one made in the background

name: DM_VK_GPL_GIVEUP
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, live, 3) graphics pipeline libraries are turned off for the run after n refused pre-rasterization libraries (pipelines are then made whole)

name: DM_VK_GPL_PROBE
meaning: `1` (Android, live, off) the first refused pre-rasterization library runs a probe that makes it again with one thing changed at a time and adopts what works; a one-off diagnostic run (it makes ~11-13 libraries on the replay thread: a 1-6 s hitch)

name: DM_VK_GPUPROF
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, live, 0 = off) times one frame in n step by step with GPU timestamps between the full barriers: `gpu prof:` lines with the frame's GPU time by kind and the costliest steps; slows that frame a little

name: DM_VK_GPUPROF_LIST
meaning: `1` (Android, live, off) with `DM_VK_GPUPROF`, logs every step of the timed frame in order (source line, draws, ops, pass)

name: DM_VK_GPUPROF_SPLIT
meaning: `1` (Android, live, off) the profiled frames (`DM_VK_GPUPROF`, one in 30 when that is 0) alternate plain and split: in a split one every draw pass of the chosen size gets GPU timestamps at its start, first draw, every pipeline change and its end, run in sysmem (`DM_VK_GPUPROF_SPLIT_SYSMEM`); `gpu prof split:` lines give the largest passes' time by pipeline (vertex and fragment shader keys: ms, share, draws, indices) and the same size pass in the last plain profiled frame (`vka_gprof.c`, android/TESTING.md)

name: DM_VK_GPUPROF_SPLIT_H
meaning: `=<px>` (Android, live, 0 = any) with `DM_VK_GPUPROF_SPLIT`, only draw passes of this render-area height are split

name: DM_VK_GPUPROF_SPLIT_K
meaning: `=<k>` (Android, live, 0) with `DM_VK_GPUPROF_SPLIT`, also a timestamp every k draws of one pipeline (0: at pipeline changes only)

name: DM_VK_GPUPROF_SPLIT_MIN
meaning: `=<draws>` (Android, live, 32) with `DM_VK_GPUPROF_SPLIT`, split passes with fewer draws are only summed (the 3 costliest of the rest are reported by pipeline)

name: DM_VK_GPUPROF_SPLIT_STATS
meaning: `1` (Android, live, off) with `DM_VK_GPUPROF_SPLIT`, each group of a split pass also gets a pipeline statistics query (needs `pipelineStatisticsQuery`): per pipeline the fragment shader invocations, their count per pixel of the pass (shaded layers), ns per invocation, vertex invocations and primitives; the pass's totals in one line (no occlusion query: it would turn a discarding shader's early Z late on Turnip)

name: DM_VK_GPUPROF_SPLIT_SYSMEM
meaning: `0` (Android, live, default 1) with `DM_VK_GPUPROF_SPLIT`, split passes are not made to run in sysmem (by default an empty vertex-stage barrier inside the pass makes Turnip render it in sysmem: timestamps inside a GMEM pass are one bin's)

name: DM_VK_GPUPROF_SPLIT_W
meaning: `=<px>` (Android, live, 0 = any) with `DM_VK_GPUPROF_SPLIT`, only draw passes of this render-area width are split (`DM_VK_GPUPROF_SPLIT_H` the height)

name: DM_VK_GPU_FLOOR
meaning: `=<pct>` (Android, live, default 100) the GPU clock floor: through `VK_QCOM_queue_perf_hint` in % of the highest clock (`0` the driver's governor); without it (Turnip, other drivers) through ADPF, on for any value above 0 (`DM_VK_GPU_FLOOR_ADPF`); the cost is power ([rendering.md](reference/rendering.md#gpu-end-held-back-by-recording-and-a-clocked-down-gpu-on-the-vulkan-replay), [frame-rate.md](reference/frame-rate.md#a-gpu-clock-floor-that-follows-the-present-period-holds-a-dynamic-interval-at-its-slowest))

name: DM_VK_GPU_FLOOR_ADPF
meaning: `0` (Android, live, default 1) no GPU clock floor without `VK_QCOM_queue_perf_hint`; with 1 the ADPF session reports each frame's span and GPU time against the game's shortest period ([frame-rate.md](reference/frame-rate.md#a-gpu-clock-floor-that-follows-the-present-period-holds-a-dynamic-interval-at-its-slowest))

name: DM_VK_GPU_FLOOR_AUTO
meaning: `1` / `2` (Android, live, default 0 = the fixed floor) `1`: the floor follows each frame's span (recording start to GPU end, p90 over 30 frames) against its period, in steps of 25 % between 0 and `DM_VK_GPU_FLOOR`; `2`: the floor only while a submission with draws is on the GPU, the governor otherwise

name: DM_VK_GPU_FLOOR_HI
meaning: `=<ms>` (Android, live, default 2) `DM_VK_GPU_FLOOR_AUTO=1` raises the floor a step when the span's p90 is within that many ms of the period

name: DM_VK_GPU_FLOOR_KGSL
meaning: `0` (Android, restart, default 1) no GPU clock floor through KGSL (a power constraint on the queue's kernel context, for drivers without `VK_QCOM_queue_perf_hint`: Turnip on Adreno); the ADPF floor then ([frame-rate.md](reference/frame-rate.md#a-gpu-clock-floor-that-follows-the-present-period-holds-a-dynamic-interval-at-its-slowest))

name: DM_VK_GPU_FLOOR_LO
meaning: `=<ms>` (Android, live, default 5) `DM_VK_GPU_FLOOR_AUTO=1` lowers the floor a step when the span's p90 is more than that many ms below the period (at most every 60 frames)

name: DM_VK_GPU_FLOOR_LOG
meaning: `1` / `2` (Android, live, off) `1` logs each change of the automatic GPU clock floor (frame, span p90, period); `2` also every floor the queue is given

name: DM_VK_GPU_FLOOR_PERIOD
meaning: `=<ms>` (Android, live, default 0 = the game's shortest period: the shortest present period it asked for, at most 16.7 ms) the period every GPU clock floor aims at (`DM_VK_GPU_FLOOR_AUTO=1`, the ADPF floor); `33.3` the cap before 2026-11-05

name: DM_VK_GS_CLAIM
meaning: `0` (Android, restart, on) geometry shaders' memory writes are not put under a per-primitive claim (`vka_spv_gs_claim`): they are repeated by the device's runs of each primitive

name: DM_VK_GS_SPV
meaning: `=<file>` a geometry shader SPIR-V module `t_android_spvpatch` runs the memory write claim rewrite on and checks

name: DM_VK_HANG_EXIT
meaning: `0` (Android, live, 1) after a GPU hang the game runs on without the GPU instead of the host exiting

name: DM_VK_HANG_S
meaning: `=<s>` (Android, live, default 6; at least 0.5) the seconds a fence may stay unreached before a GPU hang is declared

name: DM_VK_HOOKDIR
meaning: `=<folder>` (Android, restart) where libadrenotools' hook libraries are for `DM_VK_DRIVER`; default the folder `libnxhost.so` was loaded from (inside the APK)

name: DM_VK_IMGMEM
meaning: (Android, live: images made from then on, on) images under 4 MiB that the driver does not want dedicated share 64 MiB blocks of their memory type (vka_imgmem.c, exact 256-byte units, first fit; the ctl stats' `image memory:` line); `0` gives every image its own VkDeviceMemory as before (Mario Kart World ran out of allocations that way)

name: DM_VK_IMG_ALIAS
meaning: `0` (Android, live: the next binding, on) storage bindings as before: an integer one over a colour image of 4-byte texels of another class gets no R32_UINT / R32_SINT view (Ocarina of Time's AA pass d17eefaff4f0bc23 ORs blend weights into an RGBA8 image), a float one over an integer image (f8965bffbdf51d78 binding 3, R16G16_UINT) no view of the image's own format, and a view format the image's list lacks is only learned, not remade into its list (`vka_tex.c` id_view, img_remake): such bindings read as unbound

name: DM_VK_IMG_SLOTS
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, restart, 0: the device's limit, at most 65536) caps the storage-image table of the bindless set at n slots (64 bytes of descriptor memory each on Turnip); an image ID past it is logged once (`beyond the table`) and its slot is never written: a shader indexing past the table is undefined (a GPU fault is possible), so keep n above the game's highest ID ([memory.md](reference/memory.md))

name: DM_VK_IMG_UPGRADE
meaning: `0` (Android, live: the next binding, on) a texture bound as a shader image without NVN's IMAGE flag is no longer remade with storage use, and an image registration no longer counts as image intent

name: DM_VK_LC_GLOBAL
meaning: (Android, restart, on) the recording thread's address lookup cache lives in a global the first recording thread owns, not in TLS (a dlopen'ed library's `__thread` access goes through the TLS resolver: 8 % of the replay thread); `0` TLS for every thread

name: DM_VK_LOD_BIAS_MIN
meaning: `=<bias>` (Android, samplers made from then on, off) raises a guest sampler's LOD bias under it to it (`0`: no negative bias, which sharpens textures for an upscaler and shimmers at a low render size without it); each distinct bias is logged once (`sampler LOD bias … first seen`)

name: DM_VK_LOG
meaning: `=1` logs Vulkan object creation in the Vulkan-on-Metal layer

name: DM_VK_MAPS_CACHE
meaning: (Android, on) placing and giving back memory pools take the page protections from a snapshot of /proc/self/maps, read again only for a range whose 256 KiB blocks changed since (this library's mmap / munmap / mprotect / mremap mark them; a pool swap marks its range only when it may not have put the protections back); answers from the snapshot are checked against the text (the first 16, then every 64th). `0` reads the text each time (1-5 ms a pool on the phone)

name: DM_VK_MEMLOG
meaning: `=<MiB>` (Android, default 512, `0` off): a `memory:` log line each time the replay's placed pools, images and scratch memory have taken that much more (allocations counted, frees not) since the last line

name: DM_VK_MEM_LOCK_WHOLE
meaning: `1` (Android, restart): a memory pool placement holds the segment table's write lock for its whole duration, as before 2026-11-03 (the replay and the game's NVN calls wait for it: DKB's 300-500 ms loading hitches); for A/B only

name: DM_VK_MESH
meaning: `0` (Android, restart, on) leaves VK_EXT_mesh_shader off: NVN2 task and mesh shaders are refused and their draws (nvnCommandBufferDrawMeshTasks) skipped, as on a device without the task and mesh stages

name: DM_VK_MIPDROP
meaning: `1` (Android, live, 0; Ocarina of Time 1 in its profile) under memory pressure (`DM_VK_MIPDROP_AVAIL_MB`) a texture whose content is its storage (tracked, or uploaded once: `DM_VK_MIPDROP_FILL`), block-compressed (IMAGE and COMPRESSIBLE flags taken: `DM_VK_MIPDROP_IMAGE`, `DM_VK_MIPDROP_COMPRESSIBLE`), 2D / 2D array / cube, at least `DM_VK_MIPDROP_MIN` texels a side and with more levels than it drops, is made without its finest `DM_VK_MIPDROP_LEVELS` levels (about 3/4 less image memory each; sampled blurrier, an explicit level, texel fetch or size query sees the image's levels), and idle ones are made again so (`DM_VK_MIPDROP_IDLE_S`, `DM_VK_MIPDROP_SHRINK_MB`); a copy or clear into one, or a copy from one, makes it whole again first; `2` always, without pressure (`vka_tex.c` "Mip drop"; `mip drop:` lines and the `memory:` line's tail, with `mip drop while on`: new images under pressure by path and the reason each kept its finer levels) ([memory.md](reference/memory.md))

name: DM_VK_MIPDROP_AVAIL_MB
meaning: `=<MiB>` (Android, live, 1024) `DM_VK_MIPDROP=1` counts as memory pressure while `/proc/meminfo` MemAvailable is under this (read at most every 0.5 s), and for `DM_VK_MIPDROP_HOLD_S` after

name: DM_VK_MIPDROP_COMPRESSIBLE
meaning: `0` (Android, live, 1) `DM_VK_MIPDROP` leaves textures with the COMPRESSIBLE flag whole, as before 2026-11-08; by default they are dropped too (the flag only lets the Switch's GPU keep its writes compressed; a block-compressed texture is tracked or filled only from a packaged layout, a CPU write or a fill, so its bytes are plain blocks, and a GPU write makes it whole first) (`vka_tex.c` md_levels_why; the `memory:` line's `mip drop while on` reasons)

name: DM_VK_MIPDROP_FILL
meaning: `0` (Android, live, 1) `DM_VK_MIPDROP` leaves textures whose content is uploaded once (ST_FILL: a CPU_NO_ACCESS or uncached pool, or a range the CPU flushed, such as textures a GPU copy streamed in) whole, as before 2026-11-08; by default they are dropped too: their content is their storage, read through the same upload when made whole again (`vka_tex.c` md_levels_why; never shrunk)

name: DM_VK_MIPDROP_HOLD_S
meaning: `=<seconds>` (Android, live, 60) how long `DM_VK_MIPDROP`'s pressure lasts after the last MemAvailable reading under `DM_VK_MIPDROP_AVAIL_MB` (the low-memory killer's kills of other apps lift it for a moment during a load)

name: DM_VK_MIPDROP_IDLE_S
meaning: `=<seconds>` (Android, live, 10) an image `DM_VK_MIPDROP` shrinks had no lookup for this long, in seconds of submitting (bindless samples are no lookups)

name: DM_VK_MIPDROP_IMAGE
meaning: `0` (Android, live, 1) `DM_VK_MIPDROP` leaves block-compressed textures with the IMAGE flag whole, as before 2026-11-08; by default they are dropped too (no block-compressed format is a storage image on Vulkan here, and a shader-image binding or registration makes a dropped image whole first). Uncompressed textures stay whole either way (texelFetch or an explicit level would read the wrong level)

name: DM_VK_MIPDROP_LEVELS
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, live, 1; 0 none) the finest levels `DM_VK_MIPDROP` leaves out (at most all but one); each level left out is about 3/4 of what remains

name: DM_VK_MIPDROP_MIN
meaning: `=<texels>` (Android, live, 256) `DM_VK_MIPDROP` leaves textures smaller than this on either side whole

name: DM_VK_MIPDROP_RESTORE_AVAIL_MB
meaning: `=<MiB>` (Android, live, 1536) `DM_VK_MIPDROP_RESTORE_MB` makes dropped images whole again only while MemAvailable is at least this

name: DM_VK_MIPDROP_RESTORE_CALM_S
meaning: `=<seconds>` (Android, live, 15) `DM_VK_MIPDROP_RESTORE_MB` starts once `DM_VK_MIPDROP`'s pressure has been off this long

name: DM_VK_MIPDROP_RESTORE_MB
meaning: `=<MiB>` (Android, live, 0 = off; Ocarina of Time 32 in its profile) with `DM_VK_MIPDROP=1`, once the pressure is over (`DM_VK_MIPDROP_RESTORE_CALM_S`, `DM_VK_MIPDROP_RESTORE_AVAIL_MB`) images mip drop made without their finer levels and in use (a lookup or a GPU index within `DM_VK_MIPDROP_IDLE_S`) are made whole again from their storage, at most this many MiB of image memory a second

name: DM_VK_MIPDROP_SHRINK_MB
meaning: `=<MiB>` (Android, live, 64; 0 none) the image memory `DM_VK_MIPDROP` makes again without finer levels at most each second of submitting (each one uploaded again from its storage)

name: DM_VK_NANSCAN
meaning: `1` / `2` (Android, restart, needs push descriptors) after every render pass scans the float colour attachments for NaN / infinite texels and logs the passes with any (frame, attachment, shaders); `2` also splits passes to find the draw (`DM_VK_NANSCAN_STEP`, `_DRAWS`, `_SERIAL`); `3` scans no passes, only `DM_VK_NANSCAN_CS`'s dispatches (the two share a submission's 1024 results); not for play

name: DM_VK_NANSCAN_CS
meaning: `=<key>[,<key>…]` / `all` (Android, restart) with `DM_VK_NANSCAN=1`, `2` or `3` (dispatch scans only), after each dispatch of those compute shaders (hex keys, at most 16) scans level 0 of every image it binds (storage images it writes, textures it samples): float formats for NaN, infinite, all-zero and big (a component >= 256) texels and the largest component, `R32_UINT` images decoded as RGB9E5; logs each binding once, then each scan whose verdict changes (and every 120th)

name: DM_VK_NANSCAN_DRAWS
meaning: `=<from>-<to>` (Android, restart) with `DM_VK_NANSCAN=2`, split only the game's passes whose index is in that range (default all)

name: DM_VK_NANSCAN_DUMP
meaning: `=<format>x<width>` (Android, live: read at use) with `DM_VK_NANSCAN`, writes level 0 of ASTC textures of that format (hex) and width to `DM_TEMP` (`nan-<serial>-<format>-<w>x<h>.blk`, at most 64); set at all, also dumps the ASTC textures a NaN pass's draws sample

name: DM_VK_NANSCAN_FS
meaning: `=<key>` (Android, restart) with `DM_VK_NANSCAN`, a fragment shader key (hex) whose draw, once a frame, has its inputs scanned for NaN / infinite texels

name: DM_VK_NANSCAN_SERIAL
meaning: `=<serial>` (Android, restart) with `DM_VK_NANSCAN=2`, split only passes into the image of that texture serial (default any)

name: DM_VK_NANSCAN_STEP
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, restart, default 64) with `DM_VK_NANSCAN=2`, the pass is ended and scanned after every n draws

name: DM_VK_NDSR_STANDIN
meaning: `1` (Android, live; default 0; the OoT profile 0400486024DEC000 sets it in `host_env`) agl's NDSR upscaler network `d99fbeeb53d38847` is not run: its output image gets the network's input sampled bilinearly at each texel's place (from the network's own constants: output origin, extent, tile, UV step) and squared, one small compute pass; its pipeline is not made ahead. Logs `NDSR stand-in: <in WxH format> -> <out WxH format>` once per output image; a dispatch whose bindings do not fit runs the network with a `[RED]` line. Softer picture than the network's ([shaders.md](reference/shaders.md#agls-ndsr-upscaler-replaced-by-a-bilinear-stand-in-on-the-vulkan-replay))

name: DM_VK_NDSR_STANDIN_AA
meaning: `1` (Android, live; default 0; the OoT profile 0400486024DEC000 sets it in `host_env`) with `DM_VK_NDSR_STANDIN`: the stand-in reads the image the game's AA blend `a335c1db6270c355` wrote in this frame (SMAA weights from `d17eefaff4f0bc23`, square root packed as RGB9E5): its own input when that is the same image, else a335c's output in the input's view format; with no a335c dispatch in the frame, the input as before (`vka_draw.c` ndsr_standin). Logs `NDSR stand-in AA: …` when the case changes. In Ocarina of Time d99's input is a335c's output texture each frame (session-2026-11-07 aa/WIRE.md)

name: DM_VK_NDVE_DIRECT
meaning: `0` / `1` (Android, live; default 1) the movie library's NDVE network (NintendoSDK movie) is not run: after its colour conversion its dispatches are not recorded and its last pass is a linear blit of the converted frame into the movie output; its pipelines are never made. `0` runs the network ([shaders.md](reference/shaders.md#the-movie-librarys-ndve-network-scaled-instead-of-run-on-the-vulkan-replay))

name: DM_VK_NOVIEW_LOG
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, live, 64) how many distinct (shader key, binding) pairs get a line when a bound texture ID has no view: the "has no view" `[RED]` line or the 2D-in-3D / cube fallback line, one per pair (at most 128; the `[RED]` line was once counted per occurrence, so one binding that misses every frame took all 8)

name: DM_VK_PASS_CLEARS
meaning: `0` (Android, live: the next submission, 1) clears of the bound targets are made outside the render pass instead of inside the pass over them (each such clear then ends the pass)

name: DM_VK_PASS_KEEP
meaning: `0` (Android, live: the next submission, 1) a render target change ends the open pass at once instead of only when the next draw's targets differ

name: DM_VK_PCACHE
meaning: `=<file>` (Android, restart) the Vulkan pipeline cache file; `0` no file; default `$DM_TEMP/vk_pipelines.bin` (`vk_pipelines-<driver>.bin` with a custom driver); the replayer does not take it from a capture

name: DM_VK_PCACHE_MIN_S
meaning: `=<s>` (Android, live, 0 = off; Ocarina of Time 120 in its profile) the pipeline cache file is saved at most every s seconds (the saves at the end of the run, at suspend and at the shader library check stay at once); a pipeline the driver reports as a pipeline cache hit is not counted, the optimized copy of a linked pipeline asks for no save of its own, and no save starts during a burst (`DM_VK_PCACHE_QUIET_S`) unless the oldest unsaved pipeline is 4 s periods old; each save logs its bytes and the run's total

name: DM_VK_PCACHE_QUIET_S
meaning: `=<s>` (Android, live, 10) with `DM_VK_PCACHE_MIN_S` a burst that puts a save off: prewarm threads still running, asynchronous or optimizer jobs queued, or a pipeline made within this many seconds

name: DM_VK_PCACHE_SAVE_MS
meaning: `=<ms>` (Android, live, 1000; 0 = only the DM_VK_PCACHE_SAVE_S timer) the pipeline cache file is saved at once, on its saver thread, when the pipelines and libraries made since the last save took ms of creating (a slow compile is not lost when Android ends the app)

name: DM_VK_PCACHE_SAVE_S
meaning: `=<s>` (Android, live, 20; at least 1) the pipeline cache file is saved at most every s seconds while new pipelines are made (the save at the end of the run and at suspend is forced)

name: DM_VK_PLACED
meaning: `0` (Android, restart, on) memory pools stay anonymous memory instead of placed Vulkan memory, so the GPU sees none (draws then default off, `DM_VK_DRAW`)

name: DM_VK_PLACE_GRANULE_MB
meaning: `=<MB>` (Android, read once, 16) the part size of a memory pool placed by parts (`DM_VK_PLACE_PART_MB`): only the parts the GPU is given an address in become placed memory ([memory.md](reference/memory.md))

name: DM_VK_PLACE_LAZY
meaning: `0` (Android, read once, on) every memory pool is placed when it is made, instead of when the GPU is first given an address in it ([memory.md](reference/memory.md))

name: DM_VK_PLACE_PART_MB
meaning: `=<MB>` (Android, read once, 1024; `0` whole pools, as before) memory pools of at least this size are placed by parts of `DM_VK_PLACE_GRANULE_MB` instead of whole ([memory.md](reference/memory.md))

name: DM_VK_PLACE_SHADER_POOLS
meaning: `0` (Android, read once, default 1; Ocarina of Time 0 in its profile) NVN SHADER_CODE memory pools are not placed for their address or a buffer object over them (program addresses: the host reads shader code on the CPU), only for a recorded command naming an address in them (binds, draws, copies, reports) or a texture over them (`hle_nvn.c` "Shader-code pools"; [memory.md](reference/memory.md)). A shader dereferencing a raw pointer into such a pool would read the sink: `DM_VK_SHPOOL_LOG` first

name: DM_VK_PLACE_SPAN
meaning: `0` (Android, read once, default 1) a memory pool placed by parts (`DM_VK_PLACE_PART_MB`) stays one buffer a part, as before: by default its first part makes one sparse residency buffer over the pool, each part's memory is bound into it too, and lookups answer with it across contiguous parts (a storage buffer reaches past a part's end; vka_mem.c "Span buffers"); needs sparse residency buffers on the queue (`sparse:` line); checked once on the GPU (`span buffer check:`), off for the run when it fails

name: DM_VK_POOL_RESCAN_MS
meaning: `=<ms>` (Android, live, 0) lazy images' pool scan reads a storage buffer it read before again at most every ms milliseconds (250: as before); `0` once a frame, so a handle the game writes into a scanned buffer reads as a null slot for the rest of that frame only. The `pool-reading draws so far` line counts the texture IDs rescans queued (`vka_draw.c` `pool_scan`) ([memory.md](reference/memory.md))

name: DM_VK_PREFAULT
meaning: `0` (Android, restart, on) placed maps are not faulted in after placing; a diagnostic to measure whether the driver needs it

name: DM_VK_PRESS_BURST_MB
meaning: `=<MiB>` (Android, live, 384; 0 none) `DM_VK_PRESS_RATE` also turns the pressure on when this much image memory was made within `DM_VK_PRESS_RATE_S` (a burst MemAvailable has not shown yet), under `DM_VK_PRESS_RATE_AVAIL_MB`

name: DM_VK_PRESS_HYST_MB
meaning: `=<MiB>` (Android, live, 0; Ocarina of Time 256 in its profile) memory pressure that is on (`DM_VK_MIPDROP`, `DM_VK_SCAN_COARSE`, the `DM_VK_TEXFB` gate) stays on while MemAvailable is under `DM_VK_MIPDROP_AVAIL_MB` + this, and ends only after `DM_VK_PRESS_OFF_S` seconds in which no test held it (`vka_tex.c` mem_low). Ocarina of Time's walk sat at 0.98-1.12 GB on the 1024 MiB line; each end made 2.2-3.9k textures in a 1.4-3.2 s frame and turned the pressure on again within 1 s (session-2026-11-07 day2/D2.md)

name: DM_VK_PRESS_OFF_MB
meaning: `=<MiB>` (Android, live, 0; Ocarina of Time 64 in its profile) when the `DM_VK_TEXFB` gate turns off (the pressure is over), the deferred texture IDs that scans and readbacks want take at most this many MiB (whole size) a replay frame, the rest the next frames (`vka_tex.c` poff_take); the spread ends at the first frame that took them all. Logs `texture-use feedback: the gate's end spread …`. 0: all at once (Ocarina of Time: 4.4k textures, 640 MB, in one 2.5 s frame)

name: DM_VK_PRESS_OFF_S
meaning: `=<seconds>` (Android, live, 5) with `DM_VK_PRESS_HYST_MB`: how long memory pressure's tests must all be clear before it ends and the textures it kept back are made

name: DM_VK_PRESS_RATE
meaning: `1` (Android, live, 0; Ocarina of Time 1 in its profile) memory pressure for `DM_VK_MIPDROP`, `DM_VK_SCAN_COARSE` and the `DM_VK_TEXFB` gate also comes from the rate: while MemAvailable is under `DM_VK_PRESS_RATE_AVAIL_MB` and fell more than `DM_VK_PRESS_RATE_MB` within the last `DM_VK_PRESS_RATE_S` seconds of readings, or `DM_VK_PRESS_BURST_MB` of image memory was made in them; held `DM_VK_PRESS_RATE_HOLD_S` after (`vka_tex.c` mem_low; the `mip drop: memory pressure` line says which test). Ocarina of Time's save load went 2707 → 658 MiB in 20 s and crossed 1024 MiB 3 s before its kill (session-2026-11-07 fb/SAVELOAD.md)

name: DM_VK_PRESS_RATE_AVAIL_MB
meaning: `=<MiB>` (Android, live, 2048) `DM_VK_PRESS_RATE` looks at the rate only while MemAvailable is under this

name: DM_VK_PRESS_RATE_HOLD_S
meaning: `=<seconds>` (Android, live, 20) how long pressure `DM_VK_PRESS_RATE` turned on lasts after the last reading that met its test (the absolute test keeps `DM_VK_MIPDROP_HOLD_S`)

name: DM_VK_PRESS_RATE_MB
meaning: `=<MiB>` (Android, live, 400; 0 none) the fall of MemAvailable within `DM_VK_PRESS_RATE_S` that turns `DM_VK_PRESS_RATE`'s pressure on

name: DM_VK_PRESS_RATE_S
meaning: `=<seconds>` (Android, live, 5) the window of MemAvailable readings (one each 0.5 s at most, 16 s kept) `DM_VK_PRESS_RATE` compares

name: DM_VK_PRETRANSFORM
meaning: `0` (Android, live: makes a new swapchain, 1) no pre-rotation: the compositor rotates the picture instead of it being drawn in the panel's own orientation

name: DM_VK_PREWARM
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, restart, 2; at most 4) threads that make the prewarm list's pipelines (`vk_pipelines.keys`, the keys of earlier runs) in the background at nice 10 when the first pipeline is made; `0` off. The replay tool sets it to 0

name: DM_VK_PREWARM_FILE
meaning: `=<file>` (Android, restart) the prewarm list's path; default `<DM_VK_PCACHE file>.keys`, else `$DM_TEMP/vk_pipelines.keys`

name: DM_VK_PREWARM_HELP
meaning: `0` (Android, live, 1) the prewarm threads make only the prewarm list, as before; on, they make the `DM_VK_PSO_ASYNC` queue's pipelines (draws skipped waiting for them) before their next key (`made by prewarm threads` in the `asynchronous:` line) ([rendering.md](reference/rendering.md))

name: DM_VK_PREWARM_KEEP
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, live: the next write, 16384; `0` no limit) the prewarm list keeps at most the newest n records when written; the oldest loaded keys (ones no recent run needed) go first

name: DM_VK_PREWARM_MAX
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, restart, 8192) the prewarm threads make at most n pipelines of the list

name: DM_VK_PREWARM_WHY
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, 64; `0` none): for the first n pipelines the frame path makes, a log line saying why the prewarm list did not have them (no record with their shaders, or the fields in which the nearest record differs)

name: DM_VK_PROF
meaning: `1` (Android, live: the next submission, off) times the draw recording path's steps (resolve, layout, pipeline, sets, vertex buffers, draw; set writes and pushes) per draw and adds them to the replay statistics line

name: DM_VK_PSO_ASYNC
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, restart, 0; at most 4) threads that make the graphics pipelines the frame path misses (a cache-only try still runs on the frame path), their draws skipped until made, so a new pipeline costs no frame wait; `0` off: the frame waits for it. Compute and mesh pipelines stay on the frame path. With GPL off (a driver that refuses libraries, as Qualcomm's on the Adreno 840) there is no cache-only try, so a pipeline the pipeline cache already holds is made in the background too and its draws skipped for a moment. The threads run at nice 10

name: DM_VK_PSO_ASYNC_NEED
meaning: `0` (Android, live, 1) the `DM_VK_PSO_ASYNC` queue is made in queue order, as before; on, the pipeline a draw was last skipped for comes first (the oldest of those), so at a load the current frame's pipelines come before those of frames already gone (`made ahead of older jobs` in the `asynchronous:` line) ([rendering.md](reference/rendering.md))

name: DM_VK_PSO_TRY
meaning: `=<0-2>` (Android, live, 1; Ocarina of Time 2 in its profile) the frame path's cache-only try before a link or an asynchronous build: 1 always, 2 only for a key the prewarm list has (an earlier run made it), 0 never; the pipeline line counts the tries left out

name: DM_VK_PUSH_DEDUP
meaning: `0` (Android, live, 1) a push descriptor update equal to the last one of its bind point is pushed again instead of skipped

name: DM_VK_PUSH_DELTA
meaning: `1` (Android, live, off) push descriptor updates write only the descriptors that changed since the last push of the same set; off until phone-checked (a driver that mishandles incremental pushes shows wrong textures)

name: DM_VK_REACH_LOG
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, live, 0) logs the first n `[reach]` details: storage and uniform buffer bindings whose bound size reaches past their placed run or that end where placed memory continues (shader key, stage, binding, kind, address, size, run), vertex streams cut short, and asks across a pool's parts; the counts are in the `[reach]` line every 5 s regardless

name: DM_VK_ROWS
meaning: `0` (Android, live: the next re-upload, 1) a tracked linear 2D texture whose storage the CPU wrote is re-uploaded whole instead of only the rows between the written bytes

name: DM_VK_RPROF
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, live: the next submission, 0 = off) one `[rprof]` line for one frame in n: the recording thread's time over that frame's submissions cut into their begin (slot wait, texture prepare: feedback readbacks, evictions, mip drop + coarse), draws (part ends and the `DM_VK_PROF` phases: resolve, layout, images, pipeline, sets, …), set parts (walk, writes: page index, table, driver segments, images; push), pool scans, dispatches, clears, copies, buffer ops, state and pass ends, and commit (pass end, writeback, feedback copy, encoder drain, upload flush, submit), with its CPU time, major faults and what is left unattributed (`vka_rprof.h`)

name: DM_VK_RTALIAS
meaning: `1` (Android, live: images made from then on, 0; Ocarina of Time 1 in its profile) a new GPU-content (ST_ZERO) image that a zero-shared one could be, of at least `DM_VK_RTALIAS_MB` of storage in a live pool, is bound at offset 0 of one allocation per guest storage start (pool, its Initialize serial, address) and create info without the extent, instead of memory of its own: textures that differ only in size over one storage are the same bytes on the Switch. One that does not fit makes a new allocation of 1.5 times the last; a new image on an allocation others hold is not cleared at its first use (Vulkan aliasing: content undefined, as the Switch's bytes read in its shape). Ocarina of Time's DEPTH32F target that changes size every frame while Link walks took 345 MiB of own memory in 110 frames (`vka_tex.c` "Guest-aliased targets", `vka_rtalias.h`; the `memory:` line's and ctl stats' `guest-aliased:`)

name: DM_VK_RTALIAS_MB
meaning: `=<MiB>` (Android, live, 4; Ocarina of Time 1 in its profile) the smallest storage of an image `DM_VK_RTALIAS` binds to its storage's allocation; `0` turns it off. An allocation under 4 MiB is a run of a 64 MiB image memory block, not a `VkDeviceMemory` of its own, so 1-4 MiB targets add no allocations to the device's count (`vka_imgmem.c` `vka_imem_bind_alias`; the `memory:` line's `K of them runs of blocks`)

name: DM_VK_RTLOG_MB
meaning: `=<MiB>` (Android, live, 0 none) logs images of at least that memory (a zero-shared one's allocation): an `rtlog new` line when one is made, `rtlog own` when a zero-shared one gets memory of its own, `rtlog gone` when it is let go (4000 such lines at most, the rest counted), with its guest storage (address, size, pool, offset), host size and kind, format, shape, flags, the path that made it (binding, table, attachment, clear, copy, other) and its creation, last write, sampling binding, lookup and GPU index frames; every 10 s an `rtlog live` table of the live ones and `rtlog overlap` / `rtlog group` lines: live images of 1 MiB or more grouped by overlapping guest storage (host MiB against the guest MiB they span, the 10 largest groups' members) and the host MiB of images a newer image's storage overlaps, of them not used since (`vka_tex.c` "Render target log")

name: DM_VK_RTWATCH_MB
meaning: `=<MiB>` (Android, live: images made from then on, 0 none; Ocarina of Time 32 in its profile) watches new GPU-content (ST_ZERO) images of at least that memory (a zero-shared one's allocation; 32 at once): a `big target:` line when one gets memory of its own and every 10 s while it lives, with what reached it since its creation (bound for sampling, cleared to zero or to another value and the value, clears to zero left out by `DM_VK_ZSHARE_ZCLEAR`, passes as an attachment, draws there with writes on, copies or blits into it, shader-image bindings) (`vka_tex.c` "Big targets")

name: DM_VK_SCAN_COARSE
meaning: `1` (Android, live, 0; Ocarina of Time 1 in its profile) under memory pressure (`DM_VK_MIPDROP_AVAIL_MB`, `DM_VK_MIPDROP_HOLD_S`) a texture only a pool-reading draw's scan named (no lookup), tracked, colour, mipmapped, 2D / 2D array / cube, at least 64 KiB, with no IMAGE, SPARSE, LINEAR or DISPLAY flag (COMPRESSIBLE: `DM_VK_SCAN_COARSE_COMPRESSIBLE`), is made provisional from its first level of at most `DM_VK_SCAN_COARSE_DIM` texels a side (its slot shows that real coarse level, never null); a GPU write, copy or attachment makes it whole at once, a lookup or the background (`DM_VK_SCAN_PROMOTE_AVAIL_MB`) promotes it within `DM_VK_SCAN_PROMOTE_MB` and `DM_VK_SCAN_FULL_MB`; single-level and smaller textures are made whole as before; `2` always, without pressure and with no background promotion (a visual check) (`vka_tex.c` "Coarse-first"; `coarse-first:` lines and the `memory:` line's tail) ([memory.md](reference/memory.md))

name: DM_VK_SCAN_COARSE_COMPRESSIBLE
meaning: `0` (Android, live, 1) `DM_VK_SCAN_COARSE` leaves textures with the COMPRESSIBLE flag whole, as before 2026-11-08; by default they are made provisional too (the flag lets the Switch's GPU compress its writes: it changes neither sampling nor layout, and storage_mode decides whether the storage is the content) (`vka_tex.c` cf_xflags; the `memory:` line's `flags by flag` and `with the COMPRESSIBLE flag`)

name: DM_VK_SCAN_COARSE_DIM
meaning: `=<texels>` (Android, live, 128) `DM_VK_SCAN_COARSE` makes a provisional image from the texture's first level whose larger side is at most this

name: DM_VK_SCAN_COARSE_FILL
meaning: `0` (Android, live, 1) `DM_VK_SCAN_COARSE` leaves textures whose content is uploaded once (ST_FILL: a CPU_NO_ACCESS, virtual or uncached pool, or a range the CPU flushed) whole, as before 2026-11-08; by default they are made provisional too, their promotion read through the same upload as their first one (`vka_tex.c` cf_levels; the `memory:` line's `not eligible` reasons and `provisional from ST_FILL storage`)

name: DM_VK_SCAN_FULL_MB
meaning: `=<MiB>` (Android, live, 48) while `DM_VK_SCAN_COARSE`'s pressure is on, the full-size scan-named images a frame makes or promotes (one larger one when it is the frame's first); a window-named texture past it is made provisional, and lookup and background promotions wait for the next frame

name: DM_VK_SCAN_PROMOTE_AVAIL_MB
meaning: `=<MiB>` (Android, live, 1536) `DM_VK_SCAN_COARSE` promotes provisional images in the background while MemAvailable is at least this and no load runs (fewer than 32 new images in each of the last 2 seconds of submitting)

name: DM_VK_SCAN_PROMOTE_MB
meaning: `=<MiB>` (Android, live, 32; 0 only GPU writes, copies and attachments promote) the new image memory `DM_VK_SCAN_COARSE`'s lookup and background promotions make at most each second of submitting (each one uploaded again from its storage)

name: DM_VK_SCRATCH_IDLE_MB
meaning: `=<MiB>` (Android, live, default 64; `0` none) how much of the replay's idle 16 MiB scratch blocks is kept for reuse; the rest (and every larger idle block) is freed, so a lower value gives host-visible device memory back to the phone sooner (`vka_dev.c` `sblk_trim`)

name: DM_VK_SHARED_SPILL_MB
meaning: `=<MiB>` (Android, default 16): the shared memory spill buffer of compute programs over the device's shared memory (`vka_draw.c` `spill_buf`); a dispatch with more workgroups than its slices runs in parts

name: DM_VK_SHLIB
meaning: `=<file>` (Android, restart) the Vulkan shader library to load; default `<module dir>/shaders/<Vulkan chain dir>/<library file>`; the replayer does not take it from a capture; `t_android_shlib` reads it for its real-library test

name: DM_VK_SHLIB_ALL
meaning: set: `t_android_shlib` checks every entry of the real library (`DM_VK_SHLIB`) instead of a sample (every 97th plus geometry, compute, task, mesh)

name: DM_VK_SHLIB_CHECK
meaning: `1` (Android, restart) when the shader library loads, builds every shader module and compute pipeline of it and logs a `shader library check:` line (made, refused, without a layout, failed)

name: DM_VK_SHOT_ALPHA
meaning: `1` (Android, live) `nxctl.sh screenshot` / `texshot` of an RGBA8 or BGRA8 texture writes its alpha channel as grey instead of its colour (a UI layer whose text is in alpha)

name: DM_VK_SHPOOL_LOG
meaning: `1` (Android, read once, off; Ocarina of Time 1 in its profile) logs each NVN SHADER_CODE pool's uses once per pool and kind (its address, buffer objects, textures, each kind of command naming an address in it) and whether it is placed for them, and a summary at presents 60, 300 and every 1800

name: DM_VK_SHUFFLE_LDS
meaning: `0` / `1` (Android, restart; default 1 on Turnip, 0 elsewhere) compute shaders take their `DMSH_VK_MOD_SHUFFLE_LDS` module (32-bit subgroup shuffles through workgroup memory) where the library has one; `0` the shuffle instruction ([shaders.md](reference/shaders.md#ampere-hmma-and-warp-shuffles-of-agls-upscaler-on-adreno))

name: DM_VK_SPARSE_DENSE_MB
meaning: `=<MiB>` (Android, live: images made from now on, default 128; `0` no cap): a sampled sparse-pool texture with no sparse residency image (its format has none, as no block-compressed format on the Adreno 840) is a dense image from the finest level whose levels take at most this much; its finer levels are left out (`vka_tex.c` `dense_floor`)

name: DM_VK_SPARSE_LEVELS
meaning: `=0` (Android, on by default) makes every sampled texture of a sparse pool an image at its full size, as before, instead of an image of only the levels where pages are mapped

name: DM_VK_SPARSE_RES
meaning: `=0` (Android, on when the device has sparse residency for 2D images) makes large sampled textures of sparse pools dense images again instead of sparse residency images bound tile by tile as the page table maps them (`dm/gfx/vk_android/vka_sparse.c`); read once

name: DM_VK_SPARSE_RES_MB
meaning: `=<MiB>` (Android, default 32): the size from which a sampled sparse-pool texture's image (from its base level) is a sparse residency image; smaller ones stay dense

name: DM_VK_SPV_DIR
meaning: `=<dir>` `t_android_spvpatch` runs the vertex input retype rewrite on every `.spv` module there and checks them

name: DM_VK_SSBO_EXACT
meaning: `1` (Android, live, read once a draw) a storage buffer descriptor covers only the size the game bound from the address rounded down to `ssbo_align`, and a `DMSH_VK_F_SSBO_BASE` shader gets no window before it (its c0 base word holds that address): the behaviour before both; by default it covers the placed run up to `maxStorageBufferRange`, and for such a shader also up to half the range before the address (NVN storage buffers are unbounded: OoT's UI text shader reads glyph records below its slot's address; docs/reference/shaders.md "Storage buffer reads below the bound address on the Vulkan replay")

name: DM_VK_STATS
meaning: `0` (Android, live, 1) no `replay up to frame` statistics lines every 300 frames; the replayer sets it to 0

name: DM_VK_STORAGE_FIRST_USE
meaning: `=0` (Android, Switch 2 games): an uncompressed texture first used as a sampled texture ID is not taken from its storage (cleared instead, the earlier behaviour); default on (`vka_tex.c` `nvn2_sampled_content`)

name: DM_VK_SUBGROUP_GS
meaning: `0` / `1` (Android, restart) `0`: the geometry stage runs one-lane subgroups; `1`: as the device reports; default 0 on Turnip (which computes subgroup operations wrong there), 1 on other drivers

name: DM_VK_SUBGROUP_PIN
meaning: `=<stage mask>` (Android, restart, default 1 = every stage that can) the stages (`VkShaderStageFlags`) whose subgroup size is pinned to the shader library's; `0` none

name: DM_VK_SYNCLOG
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, live, 0 = off) logs the game's next n waits together with each submission's recording and queueing times and timestamp reports (`sync …` lines, one clock in ms)

name: DM_VK_TEST_HANG
meaning: `=<mode>[,<ticket>]` (Android, restart; ticket default 600) at that present the copy waits for a timeline value no earlier batch signals: mode 1 the next fence, mode 2 a value nothing signals (a sure stall, to test the hang handling)

name: DM_VK_TEXFB
meaning: `=<0-3>` (Android, restart, 0; Ocarina of Time 2 in its profile) GPU texture-use feedback: the shader library's DMSH_VK_F_TEXFB modules set a bit per texture-pool ID they index (their specialization constant true, a 128 KiB bitmap at set 1 binding 3), read back after each submission with a reporting draw; `1` logs it only (`texture-use feedback:` lines and the `memory:` line: scan-named images the GPU indexed within 2 s of their creation, IDs indexed a second); `2` under memory pressure (`DM_VK_MIPDROP_AVAIL_MB`) a reporting draw's scan makes only IDs the GPU indexed lately (others held back on a 1x1 grey placeholder), any deferred ID the GPU indexed is made at the next submission, an indexed coarse-first image is promoted, and named images the GPU never wrote that no draw indexed and no CPU lookup found for `DM_VK_TEXFB_IDLE_READBACKS` readbacks, `DM_VK_TEXFB_IDLE_FRAMES` frames and 2 s are let go (`DM_VK_EVICT`; 64 MiB a second; a serial made again within 30 s is never let go by this rule again unless MemAvailable is under half of `DM_VK_MIPDROP_AVAIL_MB`); `3` the same always (a visual check). A library without the flag, or a draw with a blind pool-reading shader, keeps the scan's images (`vka_tex.c` "Texture-use feedback") ([memory.md](reference/memory.md))

name: DM_VK_TEXFB_IDLE_FRAMES
meaning: `=<frames>` (Android, live, 8; 0 no frame condition) `DM_VK_TEXFB` 2/3 lets a named image go only when none of its IDs was indexed by the GPU and no CPU lookup found it in this many replay frames (with the readbacks and `DM_VK_TEXFB_IDLE_S`); at 0.1-1 fps one frame is longer than 2 s, and with 3 readbacks and 2 s 77 % of the released images were made again within 30 s (session-2026-11-07 fb/REL.md)

name: DM_VK_TEXFB_IDLE_READBACKS
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, live, 8; 1-63) `DM_VK_TEXFB` 2/3 lets a named image go only after this many feedback readbacks (about one a frame in Ocarina of Time) with no index of its IDs, with `DM_VK_TEXFB_IDLE_FRAMES` frames and `DM_VK_TEXFB_IDLE_S` seconds

name: DM_VK_TEXFB_IDLE_S
meaning: `=<seconds>` (Android, live, 2; Ocarina of Time 30 in its profile) `DM_VK_TEXFB` 2/3 lets a named image go only when the GPU indexed none of its IDs and no CPU lookup found it for this long (with `DM_VK_TEXFB_IDLE_READBACKS` and `DM_VK_TEXFB_IDLE_FRAMES`); 2 s while MemAvailable is under `DM_VK_MIPDROP_AVAIL_MB` or `DM_VK_PRESS_RATE`'s test fired within `DM_VK_PRESS_RATE_S` (half of it, 512 MiB, is under the phone's kill line)

name: DM_VK_TEXFB_PLACEHOLDER
meaning: `0` (Android, restart, 1) a texture ID `DM_VK_TEXFB` holds back or lets go reads as the null descriptor (zeros, size 0) instead of a 1x1 grey placeholder of its view type (alpha 1; float-class single-sampled colour registrations only, the others null either way)

name: DM_VK_TEXFB_REPORT_MB
meaning: `=<MiB>` (Android, live, 0 = off; Ocarina of Time 128 in its profile) a texture ID the GPU indexed (`DM_VK_TEXFB` report or gate evidence) is made at full size instead of `DM_VK_SCAN_COARSE`'s provisional image, and a provisional image a report asked for is promoted, outside coarse-first's caps, while this many MiB a replay frame last

name: DM_VK_TEX_LAZY
meaning: `0` (Android, restart, 1) every registered texture gets its image at registration, as before; by default a sampled texture ID gets its image at the first draw that binds it, and its texture-pool slot reads as a null descriptor until a pool-reading draw's storage buffers name it (or every ID, when a pool-reading stage has no storage buffer or more than 64 MiB of them) ([memory.md](reference/memory.md))

name: DM_VK_TEX_MEMO
meaning: `0` (Android, live, 1) the recording thread looks every texture and sampler ID up again instead of reusing its memo of the last view for that ID

name: DM_VK_TEX_SLOTS
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, restart, 0: the device's limit, at most 1,048,576) caps the sampled-texture table of the bindless set at n slots (64 bytes of descriptor memory each on Turnip: the full table is 64 MiB for the process's life); a texture ID past it is logged once (`beyond the table`) and its slot is never written: a shader indexing past the table is undefined (a GPU fault is possible), so keep n above the game's highest ID ([memory.md](reference/memory.md))

name: DM_VK_TEX_TRACK
meaning: `0` (Android, live: textures made from then on, 1) textures whose storage the CPU may write are filled once instead of tracked and re-uploaded when their pages change

name: DM_VK_TWANT_KEEP
meaning: `0` (Android, live, 1) a texture ID a pool-reading draw's scan named is no longer wanted once another texture is registered at it: its slot reads null (deferred) until a scan names it again, instead of every later texture at the ID getting its image at once; a texture whose handle no scanned storage buffer holds would read null (`vka_tex.c` treg; the `memory:` line's `table wanted before` path counts the images the inherited want makes)

name: DM_VK_UBWC
meaning: `0` (Android, live: images made from then on, 1) every colour image is MUTABLE_FORMAT without a format list, as before (any view format; no UBWC compression on Adreno)

name: DM_VK_UNPLACE_REMAP
meaning: `1` (Android, experiment, off): giving back a memory pool maps its Vulkan memory again where the driver likes before moving the anonymous pages in, and frees it after them, to find out whether the Adreno driver's vkFreeMemory then leaves the guest range alone (no hole between the free and the move); a `[RED]` line says when it does not (the pool's bytes are then lost). Needs a phone test before any default

name: DM_VK_UPLOAD_BATCH
meaning: `=0` (Android, live, default 1) records a new image's first content into the submission being recorded instead of an upload batch whose staging retires on its own completion (docs/reference/memory.md)

name: DM_VK_UPLOAD_BATCH_MB
meaning: `=<MiB>` (Android, live, 64) the staging an upload batch takes before it goes to the queue

name: DM_VK_UPLOAD_INFLIGHT_MB
meaning: `=<MiB>` (Android, live, 256) the batch staging in flight above which the replay thread waits for the oldest upload batch

name: DM_VK_UPLOAD_MT
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, live, 3) helper threads (`vk-upload`) deswizzle big block-linear texture uploads with the replay thread, in runs of block rows; `0` the replay thread only

name: DM_VK_UPLOAD_MT_MIN
meaning: `=<bytes>` (Android, live, 262144) the smallest texture upload `DM_VK_UPLOAD_MT` spreads over the helper threads

name: DM_VK_VALIDATE
meaning: `1` (Android, restart) turns on the Khronos validation layer when it is installed

name: DM_VK_VB_FILTER
meaning: (Android, live, on) vertex buffers (consecutive slots in one call), the vertex input state and the index buffer are bound only when they change in the command buffer; `0` every slot every draw

name: DM_VK_VIEW_LEARN
meaning: (Android, on) a texture of another format over a live image's memory, or a view in a format the image's list lacks, is learned (format, other format, size) and kept in `$DM_TEMP/vk_view_formats.txt`; images of that format and size made from then on take the other format in their format list (`MUTABLE_FORMAT`, no UBWC for them) and are shared. Until then the texture gets its own image. `0` learns and reads nothing (such textures always get their own image)

name: DM_VK_WORKER
meaning: `0` (Android, restart, on) submissions and presents are replayed inline on the game's thread instead of on the replay worker thread

name: DM_VK_WORKER_FRAMES
meaning: `=<n>` (Android, restart, default 1) the replay worker may be at most n presents behind the game

name: DM_VK_XP_SCISSOR
meaning: `=<px>` (Android, live, 0 = off) an experiment with a wrong picture: every draw's scissor is cut to px x px pixels, to split a pass's GPU time into per-pixel and per-draw work

name: DM_VK_ZEROLOG
meaning: `=<n>` (Android): the first n textures made as zero images whose storage holds data at their first use (virtual pools left out), with their description, pool flags and whether the first use was a sample (`vka_tex.c` `storage_mode`)

name: DM_VK_ZSHARE
meaning: `0` (Android, live: images made from then on, on) every image has memory of its own, as before; on, a large image whose content is the GPU's and that nothing has written yet (dense, single-sampled, not 3D, uncompressed, not linear or a window texture) aliases one zeroed allocation per identical create info and gets memory of its own right before its first write (`vka_tex.c` "Zero-shared images"; the ctl stats' `image memory:` line counts them)

name: DM_VK_ZSHARE_ADOPT
meaning: `1` (Android, live, 0; Ocarina of Time 1 in its profile) a zero-shared image alone in its allocation takes that allocation as memory of its own at its first write (same image, its zeros its content) instead of a new image while the old allocation waits for the submission: Ocarina of Time's 12288² DEPTH16 target held 598 MiB at that moment (`vka_tex.c` img_own; the `memory:` line's `adopted`)

name: DM_VK_ZSHARE_MB
meaning: `=<MiB>` (Android, live, 4) the smallest storage of an image `DM_VK_ZSHARE` shares; `0` turns it off

name: DM_VK_ZSHARE_ZCLEAR
meaning: `1` (Android, live, 0; Ocarina of Time 1 in its profile) a colour, depth / stencil or texture clear whose value is all-zero bits into a zero-shared image is left out and the image keeps the shared memory (zeros onto the zeros it holds; its next real write gives it memory of its own, cleared to zero) (`vka_tex.c` vka_tex_zclear; the `memory:` line's `clears to zero left out`)

name: DM_VSYNC_HZ
meaning: `=<Hz>`: rate at which a host thread fires the vi vsync event when the display link does not drive it (default 60)

name: DM_WATCH
meaning: `=<s>` dumps all threads after that many seconds (SIGALRM) and turns on the stall watchdog; off unless set

name: DM_WATCH_SAMPLE
meaning: `=<path>` (Mac): when the stall watchdog fires, samples the process for 1 s with `/usr/bin/sample` and writes the thread stacks to that path

name: DM_WATCH_STALL
meaning: `=<s>`: when the frame loop makes no progress for that long (default 15 with `DM_WATCH`), logs a red line, dumps the threads and exits

name: DM_WINDOW
meaning: When set (to any value, `0` included) opens a Mac window with keyboard and controller input; unset runs headless with the guest on the current thread; the Mac launcher sets it

name: DM_WINDOW_SIZE
meaning: `<width>x<height>` (e.g. `1920x1080`) sets the game's window size, which its render targets scale with, for main builds with a profile `window_fn` row (Mac and Android; the Android launcher's Game resolution sets it); unset, empty or `original` = the game's own size

name: DM_WINDOW_TOP
meaning: `1` (Mac, with `DM_WINDOW`) orders the game window in front without activating it and keeps it above other apps' windows, so a covered window does not slow the run; `regress.py` sets it

name: DM_XCODE_DERIVED_DATA
meaning: Xcode derived data folder for `build_ipa.sh` (default `$W/build/ios/xcode-dd`); the NSP script points it into the game's build folder

name: DM_XCODE_PROJECT_DIR
meaning: Folder of the per-game Xcode project that `build_ipa.sh --prepare-xcode` makes (default `$W/xcode`); the NSP script sets it

name: DM_XV_FILE
meaning: File where the attachment validity ledger keeps the keys it disabled after a violation, read at the next launch

name: DM_YIELD_BACKOFF
meaning: `0` turns off the yield back-off; `=<cap µs>[:<start µs>]` sets its sleep cap and the run of yields after which it starts (default 250:2000)
